contract.frozen: The text of a published definition never changes.
contract.versioning: A breaking change is a new id ending .v2, never an edit to .v1.
contract.retention: A superseded version stays served for at least 90 days.
contract.revisions: Anything said about a definition after publication is a dated entry in its revisions list; body_sha256 is the hash of the frozen body (status fields excluded), so a reader can check the body never moved.
contract.does_not_assert: Every definition states what it does NOT claim, because most misuse of a metric is reading in something it never said.

agent.statement.log.v1.title: Statement log (append-only, RFC 6962)
agent.statement.log.v1.definition: A Merkle log in the shape of Certificate Transparency (RFC 6962 section 2.1) whose leaves are the signed statement-window roots, in the order they were written. Each leaf is the exact message its root was signed over (afg-statement-root:v1:...). A signed tree head (tree size, root hash, time) is published whenever the log grows, signed with the statement key over afg-statement-log:v1:<tree_size>:<root_hash>:<timestamp_ms>; every head is kept.
agent.statement.log.v1.method: SHA-256; leaf hash = SHA-256(0x00 || leaf), node = SHA-256(0x01 || left || right). /api/statements/log serves the head, every past head and the leaves; ?consistency=<m> returns the RFC 6962 proof that the current tree extends the tree of size m, and ?inclusion=<index> the audit path of one leaf. The function rebuilds the tree from the published leaves and serves nothing if it does not match the signed head.
excludes: Windows the statement job never wrote: they are absent, not back-filled.
does_not_assert: That the statements are correct: the log proves our history of roots was not rewritten after a head was seen, not that what we measured was right.
That a root is on chain.

agent.pass.v1.title: Agent Pass: a signed, three-hour statement of what the ledger checked about one agent
agent.pass.v1.unit: one signed document per issuance; valid 3 hours; revocable
agent.pass.v1.window: issue time for the live checks; the level's own as_of; the block of the newest counted payment for the pattern check
agent.pass.v1.definition: A Pass is issued for a registration when, at issue time, all of the following hold and are recorded in the body: the published liveness level is L7 or above; no harm-kind incident is open against it; it made a counted payment in the last 30 days; its newest counted payment scored none under behaviour.out_of_character.v2, or it has fewer than 3 prior payments and the check is recorded as not taken; no bound wallet is on an issuer freeze list; no bound wallet holds a standing unlimited ERC-20 approval to a plain key. The body (RFC 8785 canonical JSON) is signed with the issuer's Ed25519 key, carries issued_at and expires_at (issued_at + 3 h), and is appended to a hash-chained log together with any revocation.
agent.pass.v1.method: Checks read from the ledger's own documents (agents, incidents, freezes, approvals) and the out-of-character scorer on the agent's counted payments; signature with node:crypto Ed25519 over the canonical bytes; log entries chained by SHA-256 of the previous entry. A verifier recomputes the canonical form, checks the signature against the published key id, checks expiry against its own clock, and reads the log for a revocation of the pass id. Optionally mirrored on the ERC-8004 Validation Registry (pass/ERC8004.md) with response 100 (holds) or 0 (revoked) and a tag naming the pass and its expiry.
excludes: Registrations below L7 (nothing to check).
Any statement about the next three hours.
Any statement about the operator, the model, the host or the agent's purpose.
does_not_assert: Safety, trust, legitimacy or compliance of the agent.
That an agent without a Pass is unsafe.
That the checks are complete: they are the six listed, taken at the times listed.
assumptions: The issuer key is kept offline from the web tier and rotated by key id.
Verifiers check expiry with a clock within minutes of UTC.
The log is public and append-only; a verifier can fetch the entries since the last head it kept.
known_gaps: A payment scored major after issuance is caught only by the revocation path (within the next scoring pass), not by the Pass itself.
The pattern check uses v2 of a definition evaluated on 17 positives; its false-alarm rate is published in oochar/RESULTS-v2.md.
The on-chain mirror costs gas per issuance and publishes which agents were checked.
agent.pass.v1.intended_use: Something a counterparty can ask for before paying or hiring an agent, verify offline, and show as a badge that says what was checked and when.
agent.pass.v1.not_intended_for: A credential of identity, a credit score, a listing criterion, or a substitute for the counterparty's own policy.
agent.pass.v1.cost_to_fake: Forging a Pass needs the issuer's private key; replaying one is bounded by three hours and the log; meeting the checks in earnest costs what reaching L7 to L9 costs (rank.costtofake.v1) plus 30 days of counted payments in character, and a harm incident or freeze removes it within one revocation pass.
agent.pass.v1.threat_model: Assume the model behind an agent can be steered by text it reads (a prompt injection, a poisoned tool result, a planted memory): every signal here is measured from the chain and our ledger, never from what the agent says, and nothing here is a verdict on an agent, an operator or a person.

agent.blast_radius.v1.title: Blast radius: what a stolen agent key could move right now
agent.blast_radius.v1.unit: USD at the block of measurement, split into parts
agent.blast_radius.v1.window: one block (the latest at measurement); approvals as of the ledger's daily approvals view
agent.blast_radius.v1.definition: For one bound wallet, the blast radius is the sum of (a) its stablecoin balances (USDC, EURC, DAI, USDT) priced at the block, and (b) its exposure through standing ERC-20 approvals, counted per token as the smaller of the allowance and the wallet's balance of that token (so an unlimited approval exposes at most what the wallet holds), listed per spender with whether the spender is a contract or a plain key; plus (c) the facts that widen it without adding dollars: an EIP-7702 delegation (the delegate code controls the account) and its known family, and unpriced assets held (ETH, WETH, cbBTC) reported by symbol.
agent.blast_radius.v1.method: eth_call balanceOf on the four stablecoin contracts and the known-token list; allowance(owner, spender) for every spender the approvals view lists for the wallet, confirmed live; eth_getCode on the wallet for the 7702 designation and on each spender for its kind; research/sweepers.json for the delegate family. Exposure is capped per token and is not added to the balance total (it is a second line: 'could move' versus 'holds').
excludes: Native ETH and non-stablecoin tokens from the USD total (listed as unpriced).
Approvals the view does not know (older than 30 days or on other tokens).
Positions held in protocols (own_position payments): not a balance the key can move with one transfer.
does_not_assert: That the key is stolen or at risk.
That an unlimited approval to a router is a problem: it is how routers work; the plain-key spender is the shape to read.
The value of unpriced assets.
assumptions: balanceOf and allowance answer at the same block (one measurement).
The approvals view is complete for the last 30 days.
known_gaps: No price source for ETH, WETH and cbBTC in the lab; the production version takes a reference price with its time.
Permit2 allowances are not read.
A 7702 delegate's capabilities are read as a fingerprint, not executed.
agent.blast_radius.v1.intended_use: A number for the operator next to a canary fire or a Gate block: what rotating the key now would protect; and a fleet-wide distribution for the Desk.
agent.blast_radius.v1.not_intended_for: Solvency, creditworthiness, or any statement about the operator.
agent.blast_radius.v1.cost_to_fake: Balances and allowances are read from the chain at a block and cannot be understated by the wallet's owner; they can be reduced in earnest (revoke, withdraw), which is the point.
agent.blast_radius.v1.threat_model: Assume the model behind an agent can be steered by text it reads (a prompt injection, a poisoned tool result, a planted memory): every signal here is measured from the chain and our ledger, never from what the agent says, and nothing here is a verdict on an agent, an operator or a person.

agent.statement.root.v1.title: Statement root, one 3-hour window
agent.statement.root.v1.definition: The Merkle root over every agent statement in one window, with the number of leaves, the previous window's root, and an Ed25519 signature by our statement key over 'afg-statement-root:v1:<windowStart>:<windowEnd>:<root>:<prevRoot>:<leaves>'. Any statement can be proven to belong to its window from the root and its proof.
agent.statement.root.v1.method: Leaves ordered by agent id; sorted-pair keccak-256 hashing, the odd leaf carried up. The public key is published at /api/statements. Roots are not yet committed on chain: that needs a funded publisher key, which only the operator can create.
excludes: Windows the statement job did not run for: they are missing, never back-filled with an invented root.
does_not_assert: That a root is on chain until a transaction hash is published beside it.

agent.statement.v1.title: Agent statement, one 3-hour window
agent.statement.v1.window: one 3-hour UTC window, published three to six hours after it closes so the payment scan has finished it
agent.statement.v1.definition: For one ranked agent (L7 or above) and one window: payments out (count and USDC, as 6-decimal base units), split into spend (counted) and routing hops, which must add up to the outflow; what left the agent's control; income in; and the open detection kinds on its wallet. Fields we do not observe are omitted, never zero-filled. Each statement carries the hash of the agent's previous statement (prevHash), so the history cannot be rewritten without breaking the chain.
agent.statement.v1.method: Canonical JSON (keys sorted, numbers as decimal strings), keccak-256. Built from money_events, actors and incidents by afg-statements every three hours. Leaves keccak256(agentId as uint256 || statementHash) form one Merkle tree per window (sorted-pair hashing); the root is published and signed.
excludes: Agents below L7.
Activity the payment scan had not read when the statement was written; a later correction appears in a later statement, never as an edit.
does_not_assert: That the agent is trustworthy: a statement is a dated record of what we observed.
Anything about chains other than Base.

approval.plain.30d.v1.title: Approvals from agent wallets to plain accounts, last 30 days
approval.plain.30d.v1.window: approvals in the last 30 days; allowances and balances read at the time of the run
approval.plain.30d.v1.definition: Non-zero approvals in the last 30 days from a paying agent wallet to a spender that has no contract code (or only an EIP-7702 delegation): a spender that is a key, not a program. This is the shape approval-phishing drainers use; it is also how an operator lets one of its own keys move funds. Each one is listed with its transaction in /api/approvals.
approval.plain.30d.v1.method: ERC-20 Approval events whose owner is a paying agent wallet (any Base wallet with a counted agent payment), on USDC, USDT, DAI, USDbC, EURC, WETH and cbBTC, plus Permit2 Approval and Permit events for the same tokens, read daily with eth_getLogs over the last 30 days. For each (wallet, spender, token) whose latest ERC-20 approval was unlimited (at least half of 2^256), the allowance still standing and the token balance are read at run time from Base's public node; WETH and cbBTC at the latest stored ETH and BTC price, EURC at 1.08. Spender code read with eth_getCode at run time.
does_not_assert: That the approval was phishing, or that anything was taken.

agent.pass.v2.title: Agent Pass, v2: the six v1 checks plus a 90-day memory of harm and a month in character
agent.pass.v2.unit: one signed document per issuance; valid 3 hours; revocable
agent.pass.v2.window: issue time for the live checks; the last 90 days for harm-kind detections; the last 30 days of counted payments for the pattern check; the level's own as_of
agent.pass.v2.definition: A v2 Pass is issued for a registration when, at issue time, every v1 check holds (published level L7 or above; no open harm-kind incident; a counted payment in the last 30 days; the newest counted payment scored none under behaviour.out_of_character.v2 or fewer than 3 prior payments with the check recorded as not taken; no bound wallet on an issuer freeze list; no standing unlimited ERC-20 approval to a plain key) and, in addition, no harm-kind detection or incident (drain_pattern, test_then_drain, address_poisoning_loss, bind_closed_after_nft_transfer) was logged against the agent in the last 90 days, open or closed, and no counted payment of the last 30 days scored notable or major under behaviour.out_of_character.v2. Body, signature, expiry, log and revocation as in agent.pass.v1.
agent.pass.v2.method: As agent.pass.v1, plus a read of the detections log for the agent over 90 days and the scores of its last 30 days of counted payments (pulse-oochar's payment_score rows). On the lab dataset (pass/ISSUANCE.md): 0 of 17 drained agents hold a v2 Pass (14 of 17 held a v1 Pass); 352 of 500 controls hold one (354 under v1); 68.1% of all 517 (71.2% under v1).
excludes: As agent.pass.v1.
Detections older than 90 days (the memory is bounded on purpose, so an agent can earn the Pass back).
does_not_assert: As agent.pass.v1.
That a detection in the window was a loss: a hand-off to the operator's own next wallet scores the same and counts the same; the Pass reads the ledger, not a judgement.
assumptions: The detections log is complete for the four harm kinds over 90 days, and the scoring worker has scored every counted payment of the last 30 days before issuance.
known_gaps: The 30-day pattern check inherits the signal's false-alarm rate (0.78 notable alerts per control agent-year under v2 on full data): 2 of the 354 controls v1 passed (a third already failed v1's in_character) control agents a month lose the Pass for a payment that was theirs to make.
A revoked Pass restarts the 90-day clock under this draft; whether it should is open.
agent.pass.v2.intended_use: As agent.pass.v1, for counterparties that want the statement to remember a drain for a season rather than three hours.
agent.pass.v2.cost_to_fake: As agent.pass.v1, plus 90 clean days after any detection: a drained or draining registration cannot hold the Pass again until a quarter has passed without a harm-kind detection, and a new registration needs 30 days of counted payments in character before its first v2 Pass.
agent.pass.v2.threat_model: Assume the model behind an agent can be steered by text it reads (a prompt injection, a poisoned tool result, a planted memory): every signal here is measured from the chain and our ledger, never from what the agent says, and nothing here is a verdict on an agent, an operator or a person.

On 12 Oct 2026 it was about $10,000 across 440 wallets: agent wallets keep little float, so the exposure is wide and shallow, and deepens whenever they are refilled.
approval.unlimited.usd.v1.method: ERC-20 Approval events whose owner is a paying agent wallet (any Base wallet with a counted agent payment), on USDC, USDT, DAI, USDbC, EURC, WETH and cbBTC, plus Permit2 Approval and Permit events for the same tokens, read daily with eth_getLogs over the last 30 days. For each (wallet, spender, token) whose latest ERC-20 approval was unlimited (at least half of 2^256), the allowance still standing and the token balance are read at run time from Base's public node; WETH and cbBTC at the latest stored ETH and BTC price, EURC at 1.08.
excludes: Balances of tokens the wallet did not approve.
does_not_assert: That the money is at risk from a specific spender: most spenders are routers, escrows and lending pools.

bankr.creatorfees.v1.title: Bankr creator fee share, cited
bankr.creatorfees.v1.definition: The creator's portion of lifetime fees across indexed launches, as computed and published by Bankr's own fee endpoint.
bankr.creatorfees.v1.method: Their number. Summed from their endpoint, not reproduced by us.
excludes: Launches with no fee record.
does_not_assert: That the creator claimed it. The endpoint reports both claimable and claimed, and this is the earned figure.

approval.unlimited.wallets.v1.title: Agent wallets with a standing unlimited approval
approval.unlimited.wallets.v1.window: approvals in the last 30 days; allowances and balances read at the time of the run
approval.unlimited.wallets.v1.definition: Distinct paying agent wallets with at least one ERC-20 approval, given in the last 30 days, that is still unlimited when read: the spender can move the wallet's whole balance of that token without asking again.
approval.unlimited.wallets.v1.method: ERC-20 Approval events whose owner is a paying agent wallet (any Base wallet with a counted agent payment), on USDC, USDT, DAI, USDbC, EURC, WETH and cbBTC, plus Permit2 Approval and Permit events for the same tokens, read daily with eth_getLogs over the last 30 days. For each (wallet, spender, token) whose latest ERC-20 approval was unlimited (at least half of 2^256), the allowance still standing and the token balance are read at run time from Base's public node; WETH and cbBTC at the latest stored ETH and BTC price, EURC at 1.08.
excludes: Unlimited approvals given more than 30 days ago (not read).
Permit2 allowances (their amounts and expiries differ; counted in the document, not here).
does_not_assert: That the spender will move anything. A standing approval is exposure, not a loss.

bankr.feerate.v1.title: Share of Bankr launches with any fee record
bankr.feerate.v1.definition: Indexed launches with a fee record above zero, divided by the launches we have actually asked the fee endpoint about.
bankr.feerate.v1.method: The denominator is ASKED, never indexed. Dividing by the indexed count would fold “we have not got round to asking” into “earned nothing”, which are different facts and only one of them is about Bankr.
excludes: Launches not yet asked about.
does_not_assert: A complete count. Bankr's batch endpoint sometimes omits a token that its own per-token endpoint shows did earn fees, on both chains and at any launch age, so the share is an under-count; how often is re-measured on every run.

A stable property of Bankr launches. The share varies several-fold by launch week and by chain, so it describes the indexed window only. Nor is it a floor: an earlier version of this definition said so, on the theory that a newest-first walk skews young, and the data disproved it - older launch weeks earn fees less often. Withdrawn 2026-09-14.
That the fee-earning launches are typical. Fees are extremely concentrated — a single token can be a third of the total — so no average here describes a real launch.

bankr.deployers.v1.title: Distinct Bankr deployers
bankr.deployers.v1.definition: Distinct deployer addresses across the indexed launches, as published in the operator's registry rows.
bankr.deployers.v1.method: Read from the registry's deployerAddress field.
excludes: Rows with no deployer published.
does_not_assert: That a deployer is an agent, or that it is distinct from the fee recipient.

bankr.launches.v1.title: Bankr launches indexed
bankr.launches.v1.definition: Distinct token addresses read from Bankr's own public launch registry.
bankr.launches.v1.method: We page their canonical discover feed, which they pointed us to publicly, and store the row. Membership is read from the operator's registry, never inferred from a hook, a beneficiary or a token-address suffix.
excludes: Launches the registry has not published.
Pages beyond the walk's current cursor position, which is published beside the count.
does_not_assert: That a launch is an agent. A token launch is a token launch, and none of these rows enters this site's actor count.
A complete census of Bankr launches. It is what their feed had returned to us by the timestamp beside it.

bankr.tosellers.v1.title: Bankr fee recipient payments to a named seller
bankr.tosellers.v1.definition: Payments from a registry fee recipient to an address in our named-seller set. This is the metric that decides whether the fee-to-compute loop closes.
bankr.tosellers.v1.method: Verified payments only, joined to the x402 recipient set. The loop is reported as closing if and only if this is above zero.
excludes: Pass-through hops.
Payments to addresses we cannot name as sellers.
does_not_assert: That a zero disproves the loop. It means unmeasured. See the scan-scope figure published with it.
The value of compute bought. It counts payments, not dollars.

bankr.platformfees.v1.title: Bankr platform fee share, cited
bankr.platformfees.v1.definition: The platform's portion of lifetime fees across indexed launches, as computed and published by Bankr's own fee endpoint.
bankr.platformfees.v1.method: Their number. Summed from their endpoint, not reproduced by us.
excludes: Launches with no fee record.
does_not_assert: Bankr's revenue. It is the platform share on the launches we have indexed and asked about, which is a subset of theirs.

bankr.withfees.v1.title: Bankr launches with any fee record
bankr.withfees.v1.definition: Indexed launches for which the operator's fee endpoint returns a record with total fees above zero.
bankr.withfees.v1.method: Batched against their public token-fee-summary endpoint. A token the endpoint has nothing for is simply omitted from the response, and we record that omission rather than treating it as zero-by-assumption.
excludes: Launches not yet asked about — the asked count is published beside this one.
does_not_assert: That the remaining launches earned nothing. It asserts the operator's endpoint has no fee record for them.
A rate over all launches unless you divide by the asked count, not the indexed count.

bankr.payingrecipients.v1.title: Bankr fee recipients observed paying
bankr.payingrecipients.v1.definition: Base fee recipients from the registry that our own payment scan has observed making a payment, after pass-through routing hops and pre-registration history are removed.
bankr.payingrecipients.v1.method: Join the registry's fee recipients against our verified payment set. This is the half of the fee-to-compute loop that only we can check.
excludes: Pass-through hops.
Payments before the payer's identity existed.
Chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: THAT A ZERO MEANS THEY NEVER PAY. Our payment scan follows wallets bound to identities in this graph and nothing else, so a fee recipient outside that set cannot appear here whatever it does with its money. The width of the scan is published beside this number for exactly that reason.
That an observed payment bought compute. That is the separate named-seller metric.

bankr.recipients.v1.title: Distinct Bankr fee recipients
bankr.recipients.v1.definition: Distinct fee recipient addresses across the indexed launches, as published in the operator's own registry rows.
bankr.recipients.v1.method: Read from the registry's feeRecipientAddress field, which was populated on every row we have seen.
excludes: Rows with no fee recipient published.
does_not_assert: That the address collected anything. It is the address named to collect.
That one address is one person. A single operator can hold many, and many launches can share one.

bankr.totalfees.v1.title: Bankr launch fees, cited
bankr.totalfees.v1.definition: Sum of lifetime total fees across indexed launches, as computed and published by Bankr's own fee endpoint.
bankr.totalfees.v1.method: THIS IS THEIR NUMBER, NOT OURS. We batch their endpoint and add up what it returns. We did not reproduce the fee accounting from chain data and we do not present this as a measurement of ours — the _cited suffix in the metric name is there so the label survives being quoted out of context.
excludes: Launches the endpoint has no record for.
Launches not yet asked about.
does_not_assert: Our own verification. An independently measured figure would be named without _cited, and this one is not.
That fees were withdrawn, spent, or converted into anything. Accrual is not a payment.
That the USD total only rises. It is Bankr's USD valuation, which moves with prices, so it can dip slightly when ETH falls even though fees earned in token units only rise.
A complete total. Bankr's batch endpoint sometimes omits tokens that did earn fees, so the total is an under-count.
Anything about this site's own spending headline, which excludes every number on this page.

behaviour.out_of_character.v1.title: Out-of-character payment, v1: a score with reasons, measured against the agent's own past
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.unit: per counted payment: a score in [0, ∞) with public reasons and a level (none, notable at 0.9, major at 1.4); per agent: collective change labels
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.window: the agent's whole counted-payment history before the payment under test (past only); block-pinned code reads
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.definition: For one counted payment by one registered agent, the score is the sum of fixed private weights over the public reasons that hold, each computed from the agent's earlier counted payments and facts at the block of the payment: amount out of its own distribution (robust z of log10 amount ≥ 3.5), a never-paid payee at a large amount (z ≥ 2.5), a never-paid plain key, a 7702-delegated payee, a never-paid payee nobody else on the ledger pays (≥ $50), off its own hourly rhythm, an unusually fast follow-up, a burst, an approval or delegation change in the last 24 hours, a small probe followed by a large payment to the same new payee, a poisoning look-alike payee, and (Watch only) a payee frozen or forwarding to a frozen address. Collective change per agent is a one-sided CUSUM on four series and a robust BOCPD on log amounts, with fixed parameters.
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.method: Features F1–F10 with the exact formulas, warm-ups (3, 8, 8, 10 prior payments), CUSUM (k, h) and BOCPD (hazard 1/50) parameters in docs/definitions/behaviour.out_of_character.v1.md, committed before the first run (217476c). Evaluated under a pre-registered plan: temporal split at 2026-09-15, false alarms per control agent-year first, recall on real positives, minority-class precision, synthetic positive control, do-nothing and drain_pattern baselines, rule of three on zeros.
excludes: Payments before registration, after the binding closed, self-transfers, routing hops (not counted payments).
Native ETH outflows.
Agents with fewer than 3 prior counted payments (no point score).
Inbound transfers (they feed the look-alike set only).
does_not_assert: That a high score is a loss, theft or compromise; it is a departure from the agent's own past with the reasons listed.
That a low score is in character: an agent with no history, or a history already shaped by an attacker, scores low.
Intent, identity or wrongdoing of any person.
assumptions: The agent's counted payments are complete (the ledger's own set).
Payee kind is read at the block of each payment, never at latest.
Independent payers are at least the dataset's cross-agent count.
known_gaps: Measured results (oochar/RESULTS.api.md, round 1 on capped histories): 1.29 notable alerts per control agent-year, recall 8 of 12 scoreable positives, none at major, 0 of 12 with any alert in the 24 hours before; precision 13% against the drain rule's 73%; synthetic positive control 84.3% against 84.0%.
Micro-payments out of a tight band and 7702-delegated payees (about 10% of counted payments on Base) drive most control alerts; addressed in v2.
F7 (approvals or delegation change) needs a log channel; off_rhythm cannot fire on histories under 27 payments.
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.intended_use: A pattern for a human or an operator's policy to read at payment time, beside the payee facts; the in-character check of the Agent Pass.
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.not_intended_for: A verdict, a public score, a ranking input, or a prediction of a drain.
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.cost_to_fake: An attacker who controls the agent can keep each payment inside the agent's own band and to known payees (the adaptive attacker in battery/ADAPTIVE.md), which bounds a drain to the band times the caps rather than stopping it; shaping the history first costs the attacker time and counted payments.
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.threat_model: Assume the model behind an agent can be steered by text it reads (a prompt injection, a poisoned tool result, a planted memory): every signal here is measured from the chain and our ledger, never from what the agent says, and nothing here is a verdict on an agent, an operator or a person.
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.source: afg-security-lab oochar/ and docs/definitions/behaviour.out_of_character.v1.md, 2026-10-14; production: AFG-Pulse (afg-oochar, afg-intake gate routes), 16 Oct 2026
behaviour.out_of_character.v1.status: evaluated in the private lab on 14 Oct 2026 and superseded by v2 before any production run; served for the record

bridge.follow.back_to_payer.v1.title: Bridged back to the paying wallet's own address
bridge.follow.back_to_payer.v1.chain_set: eip155:8453 (Base) as source; destination as reported
bridge.follow.back_to_payer.v1.definition: Dollars from bridge.follow.crosschain.v1 that reached the paying wallet's own address on the destination chain, either directly (the bridge reports that address as the recipient, as in bridge.follow.same_address.v1) or through a contract that passed the delivered token on to that address in the same destination transaction. The share divides by bridge.follow.crosschain.v1. Also published: the part of it for which claim tokens (vault shares, aTokens) were minted to that address in the same transaction, a position the payer holds on the destination chain.
bridge.follow.back_to_payer.v1.method: For deliveries the bridge reports to a different address, read the delivery transaction's receipt on the destination chain (public RPC endpoints for Arbitrum, Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Polygon and BNB Smart Chain) and take the first Transfer out of the reported recipient in that transaction. It counts as back to the payer only if that Transfer goes to the paying wallet's address, compared byte for byte. A Transfer from the zero address to the payer in the same transaction marks a position.
excludes: Deliveries on chains we do not read receipts for, and CCTP attestations (no delivery transaction is reported).
Anything that happens after the delivery transaction.
does_not_assert: That the same operator controls both addresses. A counterfactual smart account can sit at the same address on two chains.
That the position is still held today.
That money which went elsewhere was spent: it is only not proven to be the payer's own.

bridge.follow.candidates.v1.title: Agent bridge exits we follow to the other side
bridge.follow.candidates.v1.definition: Counted payments from a bound agent wallet on Base into a bridge contract we can follow: Across (SpokePool and routers whose receipts forward the full amount to it), LI.FI (LiFiDiamond, Permit2Proxy), Relay (RelayDepository, RelayRouterV3), deBridge (DlnSource), Circle CCTP (TokenMinter, TokenMessenger) and CCTP wrappers (CashmereCCTP, CCTPv2WithExecutor).
bridge.follow.candidates.v1.method: The counted set (no pre-registration payments, no same-transaction pass-through hops, receipt checked), filtered to recipients in the bridge map. Each address in the map carries a citable label in the counterparty label config.
excludes: Bridges without a public status API, and bridges we have not labelled.
does_not_assert: That a bridge exit is spending. It is money moving, usually to the same owner on another chain.

behaviour.out_of_character.v2.title: Out-of-character payment, v2: v1 with a USD floor, a fresh-destination feature, ledger-wide payee counts, and re-weighted probe and 7702 reasons
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.unit: per counted payment: a score in [0, ∞) with public reasons and a level (none, notable at 0.9, major at 1.4), plus the payee's ledger-wide popularity; per agent: v1's collective change labels
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.window: the agent's whole counted-payment history before the payment under test (past only); block-pinned code reads; ledger-wide payee counts as of the export
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.definition: As v1, with these fixed changes: the three amount reasons (amount out of distribution, new payee at a large amount, fresh destination at a new size) cannot fire under $20; a new reason, fresh_destination_at_new_size, holds when the payee was never paid before by this agent and the amount exceeds every earlier payment; probe_then_large alone reaches notable; the 7702-delegated-payee reason counts only beside another reason; independent payers use the ledger-wide count of distinct agents paying the payee (counted only when the payee was first seen before the payment); the ERC-20 approval half of the 24-hour change reason is computed from the ledger's approvals.
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.method: docs/definitions/behaviour.out_of_character.v2.md, committed alone before any v2 run (84de8ac), with the base rates read before registration and the reason a popularity dampener was rejected (7 of 12 harmful payments went to payees hundreds of agents pay). Evaluated under the same pre-registered plan as v1 on the full histories, with v1-on-full-data, the drain rule and do-nothing as baselines; v2 is claimed better than v1 only if its false-alarm rate per agent-year is not worse and its recall on real positives is higher.
excludes: As v1.
Payments under $20 from the amount reasons (they can still alert through the other reasons).
does_not_assert: As v1.
That a popular payee is legitimate or an unpopular one is not.
assumptions: The ledger-wide payee count is read as of the export; it can exceed what was known at the time of the payment and never understates.
known_gaps: Results: oochar/RESULTS-v2.md (filled by the registered run).
7702 delegation changes are not in the export, so the change reason is the approval half only.
The positives overlap the drain rule's own shape; the synthetic positive control and the control false-alarm rate are the independent evidence.
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.intended_use: As v1: a pattern to read at payment time; the in-character check of the Agent Pass; the signal section of a Gate policy (gate/policies/).
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.cost_to_fake: As v1; in addition, an attacker must send a first payment to a new payee under the agent's largest earlier payment (which the probe reason then watches), and cannot hide a large first payment to a never-paid key behind a wide amount band.
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.threat_model: Assume the model behind an agent can be steered by text it reads (a prompt injection, a poisoned tool result, a planted memory): every signal here is measured from the chain and our ledger, never from what the agent says, and nothing here is a verdict on an agent, an operator or a person.
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.source: afg-security-lab oochar/v2.mjs and docs/definitions/behaviour.out_of_character.v2.md, 2026-10-14; production: AFG-Pulse (afg-oochar, afg-intake gate routes), 16 Oct 2026
behaviour.out_of_character.v2.status: shadow: computed for every counted payment of ranked agents since 16 Oct 2026 (afg-oochar); nothing blocks or alerts from it; the drain_pattern detector remains the published rule

bridge.follow.crosschain.v1.title: Bridge exits delivered to another chain
bridge.follow.crosschain.v1.chain_set: eip155:8453 (Base) as source; destination as reported
bridge.follow.crosschain.v1.definition: Dollars from bridge.follow.candidates.v1 that the bridge reports as delivered on a chain other than Base (Across filled, LI.FI done, Relay success, deBridge fulfilled or unlocked), or, for CCTP, attested by Circle. Also published: the number of distinct destination chains and the share of the largest one.
bridge.follow.crosschain.v1.method: As bridge.follow.resolved.v1. The destination chain is the bridge's own field; non-EVM destinations keep each bridge's own numbering mapped to a name (Solana, Hyperliquid, Lighter, Sui, Aptos), never read as an EVM chain id. Dollars are the source-side counted value on Base, not the delivered amount.
excludes: Routes that ended on Base (bridge.follow.same_chain.v1).
Refunds (bridge.follow.refunded.v1).
does_not_assert: That the money is spent on the destination chain. What happens there next is not read here.
For CCTP, that the mint happened: Circle's attestation authorises the mint, which is a separate destination transaction we do not read.
That any of it is added to a Base figure. It never is.

bridge.follow.same_chain.v1.title: Bridge-aggregator routes that stayed on Base
bridge.follow.same_chain.v1.definition: Dollars from bridge.follow.candidates.v1 whose route, as reported by the aggregator, ended on Base: the aggregator was used to swap, and the money never left the chain.
bridge.follow.same_chain.v1.method: As bridge.follow.resolved.v1: the destination chain the aggregator reports is Base (8453).
does_not_assert: That these payments are mislabelled as bridge exits in the category split. The category describes the contract; this measures the route. Both are published.

bridge.follow.same_address.v1.title: Bridged to the same address on another chain
bridge.follow.same_address.v1.chain_set: eip155:8453 (Base) as source; destination as reported
bridge.follow.same_address.v1.definition: Dollars from bridge.follow.crosschain.v1 whose receiving address on the destination chain equals, byte for byte, the wallet that paid on Base. The share divides by bridge.follow.crosschain.v1.
bridge.follow.same_address.v1.method: Compare the bridge-reported recipient (Across recipient, LI.FI toAddress, Relay recipient, deBridge receiverDst, CCTP mintRecipient) with the paying wallet, lower-cased. Non-EVM recipients never match.
excludes: Recipients the bridge does not report.
does_not_assert: That the same operator controls both addresses. A counterfactual smart account can sit at the same address on two chains under different control.
That a different address means a different owner. Many agents bridge to their own second wallet.

bridge.follow.refunded.v1.title: Bridge exits refunded
bridge.follow.refunded.v1.definition: Dollars from bridge.follow.candidates.v1 that the bridge reports as refunded or expired: the deposit came back instead of being delivered.
does_not_assert: Where the refund went after it came back.

bridge.follow.resolved.v1.title: Bridge exits whose outcome the bridge has reported
bridge.follow.resolved.v1.definition: Dollars from bridge.follow.candidates.v1 for which the bridge's own status API returns an outcome: delivered on another chain, attested (CCTP), refunded or expired, or a route that ended on Base. The share divides by all candidate dollars.
bridge.follow.resolved.v1.method: For each source transaction on Base, one call to the bridge's public, keyless status API: Across app.across.to/api/deposit, LI.FI li.quest/v1/status (accepted only when its sending leg is that Base transaction), Relay api.relay.link/requests/v2, deBridge dln-api.debridge.finance, Circle iris-api.circle.com/v2/messages. Largest first, every two hours; pending answers re-asked hourly, not-found up to four times.
excludes: Pending, failed, not-found and not-yet-asked payments (the unresolved remainder).
does_not_assert: That an unresolved payment is lost. Most are simply not yet asked or not indexed by the bridge's API.

cctp.watched.v2.title: CCTP contract addresses watched
cctp.watched.v2.definition: How many Circle CCTP contract addresses the exit check (cctp.exits.v2) matches against, now including the TokenMinters.
cctp.watched.v2.method: Counted from the static map built from Circle's published contract reference.
excludes: CCTP deployments on chains our payment scan does not cover.
does_not_assert: That this is every CCTP contract Circle operates.

cctp.exits.v1.title: Observed agent payments into Circle CCTP
cctp.exits.v1.definition: Payments from a bound agent wallet whose recipient is a Circle CCTP TokenMessenger or MessageTransmitter — a USDC burn destined for another chain.
cctp.exits.v1.method: Match the recipient of every observed payment against Circle's own published CCTP contract addresses. Both CCTP V2 and the older V1 TokenMessenger are watched, so a zero cannot be an artefact of tracking only the new contract.
excludes: Cross-chain movement through bridge aggregators rather than CCTP directly. That is a different measurement and we have not made it yet.
Chains other than Base, because that is where our payment scan runs.
does_not_assert: That agents do not move between chains. It says only that they do not use Circle's own bridge to do it — a bridge aggregator sits among our busiest counterparties.
That CCTP is unused generally. This counts our tracked agents, not the protocol.

cctp.exits.v2.title: Counted agent payments into Circle CCTP
cctp.exits.v2.definition: Counted payments from a bound agent wallet whose recipient is a Circle CCTP contract on Base: TokenMessenger, MessageTransmitter or TokenMinter, V1 or V2. A USDC burn destined for another chain.
cctp.exits.v2.method: Match the recipient of every counted payment against Circle's published CCTP contract addresses, including both TokenMinters (verified source on the explorer). depositForBurn moves the USDC from the sender to the TokenMinter and burns it there, so the minter is where a direct CCTP exit shows up in the transfer tape.
excludes: Payments through contracts that wrap CCTP (CashmereCCTP, CCTPv2WithExecutor): the agent pays the wrapper, not Circle. They are counted as bridge exits (cp.cat.bridge.usd.v1) and followed in bridge.follow.*.
Payments before the wallet's first registration, and same-transaction pass-through hops, as for every counted payment.
does_not_assert: That the USDC was minted on the destination. A burn on Base is not a mint elsewhere; bridge.follow.* reads Circle's attestation for that.
That CCTP is used or unused generally. This counts our tracked agents, not the protocol.

cctp.exit.usd.v1.title: USD value of observed agent payments into CCTP
cctp.exit.usd.v1.definition: The summed USD value of those same payments.
cctp.exit.usd.v1.method: As above, summing the recorded USD value.
excludes: The same exclusions as the event count.
does_not_assert: That a zero means agents hold no cross-chain balances. We observe outbound payments on Base, not balances elsewhere.

cctp.exit.usd.v2.title: USD value of counted agent payments into CCTP
cctp.exit.usd.v2.definition: The summed USD value of the payments in cctp.exits.v2.
cctp.exit.usd.v2.method: As cctp.exits.v2, summing the recorded USD value.
excludes: As cctp.exits.v2.
does_not_assert: That a small value means agents hold no cross-chain balances. We observe outbound payments on Base, not balances elsewhere.

census.actors.v1.title: Registrations in the graph
census.actors.v1.definition: Every ERC-8004 registration on Base that has an actor in our graph, with its owner wallet bound by ownerOf. Since 27 September 2026 that is every registration with a non-burn owner, read daily from the registry's owner list; before, only registrations the prober had sampled.
census.actors.v1.method: Alchemy NFT API getOwnersForContract over the Identity registry, then the same actor and binding rows the prober writes, at liveness 0.
excludes: Registrations whose owner is a burn or zero address.
does_not_assert: Anything above L0 for a registration the prober has not graded and the payment scan has not read.

canary.trigger.v1.title: Canary trigger: a planted decoy was touched
canary.trigger.v1.unit: events (one per trigger per canary per observation)
canary.trigger.v1.window: continuous; evaluated every watcher pass (2 minutes) against the state recorded at the previous pass
canary.trigger.v1.definition: A canary trigger is recorded when a decoy the operator registered with us (a planted address, private key, URL, API key, tool name or x402 resource, of which we hold only the public part) shows a use that the operator never performs: a transaction sent from the key (nonce increase), code at the address (an EIP-7702 designation), an EIP-2612 or Permit2 signature used on chain, a sign-in attempt with the key, an inbound stablecoin transfer of at least $1, or a hit on the URL, key, tool or resource reported through the operator's own logs.
canary.trigger.v1.method: The watcher reads eth_getTransactionCount and eth_getCode at latest for every planted address each pass, and one eth_getLogs per stablecoin for Transfer events whose recipient is a planted address and Approval/Permit events whose owner is one, over the blocks since the last pass; URL, API-key, tool, x402 and SIWE observations are rows the operator pushes to /api/canary/ingest. A trigger is the difference from the recorded state, never a single reading. Inbound transfers under $1 are logged as dust and are not triggers. An observation the operator declared as a test beforehand (by canary id and trigger within the hour, or by transaction hash or request id) is recorded with operator_test true, written to the log and not pushed as an alert. Code at an address triggers once, when it differs from the recorded state; unchanged code is a log line. Every trigger is written to the signed statement log as a leaf whose data carries the operator id, canary id, trigger, severity, time and the SHA-256 of the evidence.
excludes: Inbound transfers under $1 (dust, including poisoning plants): logged, not triggered.
Readings taken in the first pass after registration (the baseline).
Observations the operator declared as a test before they happened (recorded and logged, not pushed).
Private material of any kind: never stored, so never read.
does_not_assert: Who used the decoy, or how it was obtained.
That the agent, its host or its model was compromised: a trigger is a pattern for a human to read.
That an untriggered canary means nothing was read: a decoy is only seen when it is used.
assumptions: The operator planted the decoy where only an intruder or a misled agent would read it, and never uses it.
The decoys are drawn from the same distribution as the real items around them (honeywords), so an attacker who holds the whole set cannot tell which is the trap.
The RPC endpoint serves latest-state reads and the last few hundred blocks of logs.
known_gaps: Permit and Permit2 use needs a log channel; on the free endpoints available on 14 Oct 2026 only the last ~4,000 blocks are served.
SIWE, HTTP, API-key, tool and x402 triggers depend on the operator's own logging and its clock.
A planted key that is swept by a bot before the first watcher pass shows as 'used before registration' and is refused.
canary.trigger.v1.intended_use: An operator's early warning that an agent's environment (memory, config, address book, tool list) was read or steered; a fact beside the Gate's decision, and an input to revoking a Pass.
canary.trigger.v1.not_intended_for: Attribution, law enforcement, public naming, or any claim about a third party.
canary.trigger.v1.cost_to_fake: To trigger a canary without reading it, an attacker must guess a 20-byte address, a 32-byte key, a 32-byte URL or key hash, or a tool name chosen from the operator's own vocabulary; the address and key spaces make that infeasible, and a URL or API-key hit needs the exact secret. To suppress a trigger, an attacker would have to stop the operator's logs or the watcher's RPC reads, which the watcher reports as a gap, not as silence.
canary.trigger.v1.threat_model: Assume the model behind an agent can be steered by text it reads (a prompt injection, a poisoned tool result, a planted memory): every signal here is measured from the chain and our ledger, never from what the agent says, and nothing here is a verdict on an agent, an operator or a person.

check.trace.v1.title: Evidence pack: where did the money go

check.trace.v1.definition: For each exit: the first hop's label, contract or key, how many agents pay it, whether an issuer froze it (issuer.freeze.v1), and whether the agent probed it first (detector.test_then_drain.v1). does_not_assert: That the deposit earned anything. It records where cash went, not what it returned.
Who operates the contract. A label describes what the code does; naming a company is a separate claim needing separate evidence, and we do not make it.

revisions.what: The window reads "all observed payments"; the base is the counted set (receipt read, no routing hops, nothing before registration), which is what the code has always used. A label-map update moves payments between categories without new payments: see /api/changepoints. pay.composition.v1 adds the parts that make the categories add up to the counted total.

cp.labelled.count.v1.title: Counterparty addresses carrying a label
cp.labelled.count.v1.definition: How many destination addresses have a label with a citable basis.
does_not_assert: That labelling is complete. It is deliberately small: an address enters only with evidence a reader can open.

cp.labelled.share.v1.title: Share of observed agent payments with a named destination
cp.labelled.share.v1.definition: Payments whose recipient we can name from a citable source, divided by all observed payments.
cp.labelled.share.v1.method: Counted from the label config. This is the honesty gauge for every category share above it: a category share means little without knowing how much of the map is still blank.
does_not_assert: That the unlabelled remainder is unimportant. By value it is the majority, because the single largest actor pays destinations we have not named.
That a labelled destination is understood. We know what the contract calls itself, not what any given payment was for.

revisions.what: Two corrections. The base is the counted set (receipt read, no routing hops, nothing before registration), not all observed payments; the code has always used the counted set. And the note that the unlabelled remainder is the majority by value is out of date: on 12 October 2026 labelled destinations took 89.7% of counted value. This share counts payments; cp.labelled.usd.share.v1 is the share by value.

cp.labelled.events.v1.title: Observed agent payments with a named destination
cp.labelled.events.v1.definition: The raw count behind counterparty_labelled_share: payments whose recipient carries a label with a citable basis.
cp.labelled.events.v1.method: Counted in the same pass as the category metrics, so the categories always sum to exactly this number.
excludes: Pre-registration and pass-through payments, like every payment total.
does_not_assert: That a labelled destination is understood. We know what the contract calls itself, not what any payment was for.

cp.known.v1.title: Distinct addresses our agents have paid
cp.known.v1.definition: Every distinct destination address across observed agent payments.
cp.known.v1.method: Counted from observed payments after the pre-registration exclusion. The full set is published.
excludes: Destinations of excluded payments.
does_not_assert: That these are sellers. Most are contracts, and we do not claim to know what a given contract does unless we can name it from a citable source.

cp.payers.l7.v1.title: Who paid this address: ranked agents and counted payments
cp.payers.l7.v1.window: all time, or the pack's dated window
cp.payers.l7.v1.definition: For one receiving address: the payments into it from wallets bound to ERC-8004 registrations that are counted (made after the paying agent was registered, and not routing hops), with first_seen, last_seen, n_payments, the counted USD, distinct paying agents at L7 or above, and the top payer's share of the counted USD. An address that only ever received routing hops is not a payee and gets no pack.
cp.payers.l7.v1.method: money_events kind PAY with to_id = the address, excluding pre_registration and pass_through rows; the paying actor's liveness and its open binding (method, confidence) from tables actors and bindings.
excludes: Routing hops (pass_through): the money passed through to someone else in the same transaction.
Payments made before the paying agent's registration.
Payments from wallets not bound to a registration.
does_not_assert: Who operates the receiving address.
That a payment bought anything: a payment is a transfer to a different address, observed on chain.

cp.labelled.usd.share.v1.title: Share of counted spending paid to a labelled destination, by value
cp.labelled.usd.share.v1.definition: USD paid to destinations in our label map, as a share of the counted total, from the composition pass (pay.composition.v1). cp.labelled.share.v1 is the same share by number of payments.
cp.labelled.usd.share.v1.method: 1 − (agent_to_agent + x402_sellers + unnamed) / total, from the same pass.
does_not_assert: That a label names a company: it describes the destination's code, with a citable basis.
That a labelled payment is understood: we know what the contract calls itself, not what any given payment was for.

cparty.classified.v1.title: Counterparties classified by code
cparty.classified.v1.definition: Addresses among the largest recipients of counted agent spending whose code we have read: contract, plain key, or key delegated to code under EIP-7702.
cparty.classified.v1.method: eth_getCode, 40 addresses per batch, within our request limits.
does_not_assert: What the contract does or who runs it.

detection.week.v1.title: Detections in the last 7 days
detection.week.v1.definition: Detections whose event time falls inside the last seven days.
detection.week.v1.method: Counted from the same log. Dated by when the event happened, not by when we noticed it, so a backfill does not make last week look busy.
excludes: Older detections, which remain in the log.
does_not_assert: That activity is rising or falling. One week is a count, not a trend.

cp.repeat.v1.title: Destinations paid by three or more different agents
cp.repeat.v1.definition: Counterparties that have received payments from at least three distinct tracked agents.
cp.repeat.v1.method: Group observed payments by destination and count distinct payers. Ranked by distinct payers rather than volume, because volume is dominated by one large actor while the number of separate agents choosing a destination cannot be faked by a whale.
excludes: Destinations below the threshold.
does_not_assert: That these are the best or busiest services. Three payers is a low bar, chosen because the population above it is still small.

detector.drain_pattern.v1.title: Drain-shaped payment, superseded
detector.drain_pattern.v1.definition: A counted payment at least five times the agent's previous largest, at least $250, to an address the agent had never paid, after at least three earlier counted payments.
detector.drain_pattern.v1.method: Read from the counted payments of each agent. v2 keeps this rule unchanged and adds the balance the payment took, read at the block before it.
excludes: Routing hops and payments from before registration.
does_not_assert: That the payment was a theft.
Anything about token drains: the rule reads stablecoin payments only.

detection.logged.v1.title: Detections logged
detection.logged.v1.definition: Every anomaly our detectors have recorded: mint bursts, retry storms, endpoints that never answer, identities that changed owner, delegations outside the allowlist.
detection.logged.v1.method: Queries over our own measurements, hourly, no external calls. Each detection is a row with a time and an evidence object. History before 2026-09-11 is carried over from open_incidents, which counted exactly these rows under a name that promised something else.
excludes: States. A low liveness score is a measurement, not a detection, and never appears here.
does_not_assert: That a detection is wrongdoing. Most of the log is mint bursts, and bulk minting is legitimate behaviour that changes what a registration count means rather than evidence of abuse.
That the log is exhaustive. It holds what these detectors can see in what we have measured.

detector.drain_pattern.v2.title: Drain-shaped payment, with the balance it took
detector.drain_pattern.v2.definition: A counted payment at least five times the agent's previous largest, at least $250, to an address the agent had never paid, after at least three earlier counted payments: the unchanged v1 rule. New in v2, every detection carries a balance reading: what the paying wallet held in that stablecoin at the block before the payment, and the fraction of it the payment took.
detector.drain_pattern.v2.method: balanceOf at block minus one through an archive-capable RPC, read once per detection and stored on it. A wallet funded and emptied inside one block is read as emptied. The fraction is evidence beside the rule; it does not filter detections yet.
excludes: Routing hops and payments from before registration, as in v1.
does_not_assert: That a payment which emptied the wallet was a theft. On synthetic data with known answers the fraction separated every planted drain from every one-off purchase; on the live ledger 39 of the 47 drain-shaped payments since February took 80 to 100 percent of the balance. Each detection says what was seen and leaves the verdict to the reader.
detector.drain_pattern.v2.source: AFG-Pulse incident detectors, Base archive RPC

cp.topshare.v1.title: Share of paying agents sharing one destination
cp.topshare.v1.definition: The number of distinct agents that have paid the single most popular counterparty, divided by the number of distinct agents we have observed paying anyone.
cp.topshare.v1.method: Counterparties ranked by DISTINCT paying actors, not by volume. Volume is dominated by one large actor — roughly two thirds of all value comes from a single registration — so ranking by it would measure that actor rather than the market. Distinct payers cannot be inflated by one whale.
excludes: Payments excluded as pre-registration.
Self-transfers.
does_not_assert: That the destination is a seller, a service, or an operator. It is an address that many agents pay. Most top destinations are CONTRACTS, and we do not read intent from bytecode.
That the agents are unrelated to each other. A single operator running many registrations would look like many payers here, and we cannot currently tell the difference.

cparty.contract.share.v1.title: Share of agent money paid to contracts
cparty.contract.share.v1.window: all time, over the top 500 counterparties by counted USD
cparty.contract.share.v1.definition: Of the counted agent spending that went to the 500 addresses receiving the most of it, the share that went to addresses holding contract code (not a plain key, not a key delegated to code under EIP-7702).
cparty.contract.share.v1.method: eth_getCode on each address, re-read monthly. A 23-byte 0xef0100 designator is a delegated key, counted as a wallet, not a contract.
excludes: Counterparties outside the top 500.
does_not_assert: What the contract is. Naming comes from the counterparty labels, which are curated with a source each.

detector.mint_burst.v1.title: Mint burst (calendar-hour rule), superseded
detector.mint_burst.v1.definition: ERC-8004 registrations minted by one address, grouped by calendar hour; a detection when twenty-five or more fall in that hour. One detection per hour.
detector.mint_burst.v1.method: Grouped by the clock hour of each mint. Reconstructed on 12 Oct 2026 from the v2 record of what it replaced.
excludes: By construction, runs that cross an hour mark, which it split into several rows: the reason it was replaced.
does_not_assert: Anything about intent or legitimacy. A burst changes what a registration count means; it is never an incident.

detector.layering_fan.v1.title: Fleet funding shape (same-amount fan-out)
detector.layering_fan.v1.definition: One ranked agent paying four or more other registered agents the same exact amount (at least $20 each) within fourteen days.
detector.layering_fan.v1.method: AMLSim's same-amount fan-out shape, run over agent-to-agent counted payments. The shape is reported once per payer, day and amount.
excludes: Fan-outs of differing amounts, which is what paying several suppliers looks like.
Payments to addresses that are not another registered agent's bound wallet.
does_not_assert: Layering in the money-laundering sense. Across 317,368 agent-to-agent payments the chain holds no cycle and no scatter-gather; every fan-out found so far is one treasury funding a fleet of its own registrations, which changes what a count of agents means. A shape, never an incident.

detector.retry_storm.v1.title: Retry storm (calendar-hour rule), superseded
detector.retry_storm.v1.definition: Counted payments from one agent to one payee, grouped by calendar hour; a detection when fifty or more of them fall inside ten minutes within that hour. One detection per hour.
detector.retry_storm.v1.method: Grouped by the clock hour of each payment. Reconstructed on 12 Oct 2026 from the v2 record of what it replaced.
excludes: Payments from before the agent was registered.
By construction, runs that cross an hour mark: the reason it was replaced.
does_not_assert: Intent. A load test and a broken retry loop leave the same shape.

detector.retry_storm.v2.title: Retry storm (a run with a ten-minute peak)
detector.retry_storm.v2.definition: A run of counted payments from one agent to one payee in which no gap between consecutive payments exceeds ten minutes, and some ten-minute span inside the run holds fifty or more payments. One detection per run.
detector.retry_storm.v2.method: A sliding ten-minute window over each payer-payee sequence gives every payment the count of payments in the ten minutes before it; consecutive payments less than ten minutes apart form a run; a run is reported when its peak count reaches fifty. Keyed on the hour the run starts, so a run the previous rule found keeps its id.
excludes: Runs whose densest ten minutes hold fewer than fifty payments: a storm spread over twenty-five minutes is not reported, by design.
Payments from before the agent was registered.
does_not_assert: Intent. A load test and a broken retry loop leave the same shape.
That the money was lost: the storm's total is reported beside it.
detector.retry_storm.v2.replaces: the calendar-hour rule in use from 2026-09-11 to 2026-10-11, which grouped payments by hour and asked whether fifty fell inside ten minutes. It missed every run that crossed the hour mark and every run with a stray payment later in the hour: 10 storm detections where the ledger holds 45, from 7 payer-payee pairs where there are 28. Measured on synthetic data with known answers (15 of 15 planted storms, plus the 8 hour-straddling ones the old rule missed, no false alarms) before shipping.

detector.test_then_drain.v1.title: test_then_drain: a probe payment, then the drain
detector.test_then_drain.v1.window: payments of the last 30 days open a detection; the whole ledger was measured before the rule was switched on
detector.test_then_drain.v1.definition: A counted payment to an address the agent had never paid before except for at most two earlier payments of at most $5 each and at most 2% of this payment (the probes), the first probe at most six hours before; the payment is at least 5 times the agent's previous largest counted payment, at least $250, after at least 3 earlier counted payments not counting the probes. The shape Reid & Harrigan (2011) documented on the June 2011 Bitcoin theft (1 BTC first, 25,000 BTC minutes later to the same address). The drain rule (detector.drain_pattern.v2) cannot see this pair, because the probe makes the payee a known one.
detector.test_then_drain.v1.method: lib/detectors.mjs testThenDrain, run hourly by afg-incidents over money_events. Measured over the whole ledger on 13 Oct 2026 before it was switched on: 5 pairs since February against 53 pairs of a probe followed within six hours by a payment 50 times larger in ordinary commerce (eval/ttd-eval-2026-10-14.json); none of the 15 drain_pattern incidents overlaps, by construction.
excludes: Routing hops, payments before registration, and payments whose receipt is not read yet.
Pairs where the large payment is below the drain thresholds.
does_not_assert: A theft: a buyer trying a service with a cent before a large order leaves the same pair. It is a shape to read, not a verdict.

detector.score.v1.title: Detector record, per rule
detector.score.v1.window: all time (fired, checked, confirmed, reversed); now (open); since the poisoning watch's first block (poisoning_adjacent)
detector.score.v1.definition: For each detector rule: fired = detections the rule logged; open = of those, live now under the incident rule; checked = fires later re-derived from stored payments and receipts by the verification job; confirmed = checked and still held; reversed = checked and withdrawn, each with its reason stored; poisoning_adjacent = fires whose wallet received an address-poisoning transfer within seven days either side, counted only for fires inside the poisoning watch's window. The poisoning watch's own record (address_poisoning_loss) counts losses and how many two independent reads confirmed.
detector.score.v1.method: Read from the detection log (table incidents), the verification records (table findings: verified_at, verification.ok, retired_reason), and the poisoning watch (tables poison_events, poison_losses). Published with every detections document, hourly.
excludes: Fires we never re-derived: they count in fired but not in checked.
Any case we cannot bind to a stored record. Known cases replayed in a research note are listed by name with their source, not added to the counts.
does_not_assert: A false-positive rate: checked is a non-random subset of fired.
That an unchecked fire was right or wrong.
That a poisoning-adjacent fire was caused by the poisoning.

detector.mint_burst.v2.title: Mint burst (a run with a sixty-minute peak)
detector.mint_burst.v2.definition: A run of ERC-8004 registrations minted by one address in which no gap between consecutive mints exceeds sixty minutes, and some sixty-minute span inside the run holds twenty-five or more. One detection per run.
detector.mint_burst.v2.method: The same sliding-window-over-runs method as the retry storm, with sixty minutes and twenty-five. Keyed on the hour the run starts.
excludes: Runs whose densest hour holds fewer than twenty-five mints.
does_not_assert: Anything about intent or legitimacy. Bulk minting is what a platform issuing identities for its users looks like. A burst changes what a registration count means; it is never an incident.
detector.mint_burst.v2.replaces: the calendar-hour rule (from 2026-09-11), which split runs at the hour mark and logged one run as several rows: 83 bursting addresses where the ledger holds 88. Rows logged by the old rule stay in the log as history; 71 runs it split or missed were added on 11 October 2026.

dop.integrators.v1.title: Distinct Doppler integrator addresses recovered
dop.integrators.v1.definition: Distinct integrator addresses read out of launch calldata.
dop.integrators.v1.method: The integrator is field 11 of Airlock's CreateParams, so it is readable when create() is the top-level call. Through an ERC-4337 UserOperation it is buried in an inner call and the launch is recorded as unattributed.
excludes: Every launch routed through account abstraction, which is the majority. This count is therefore a floor and is not a measure of how many front-ends use Doppler.
does_not_assert: That any integrator address belongs to a named product. Doppler's documentation names Zora, Paragraph, Noice and Bankr as integrators, but the on-chain addresses are not published anywhere we can cite, so we do not attach names to them.
That integrator share can be measured from this. It cannot, while most launches bury the field.

dop.nobeneficiary.rate.v1.title: Share of Doppler launches with no external fee beneficiary
dop.nobeneficiary.rate.v1.definition: Launches whose fee-beneficiary split names nobody except Doppler's own protocol address, divided by all launches carrying a split.
dop.nobeneficiary.rate.v1.method: Decode the (address, share) array emitted by the DopplerHookInitializer at launch. The protocol beneficiary is identified by appearing on essentially every launch rather than by hardcoding an address, so a redeployment does not silently break the measure.
excludes: Launches that emitted no split event — different migrator paths do not emit one.
does_not_assert: That such a launch earns nothing. It means no creator address was named in the split, not that the creator has no other claim.

dop.recipients.v1.title: Distinct Doppler launch fee recipients
dop.recipients.v1.definition: Distinct addresses named as fee beneficiaries in a launch split, excluding Doppler's own protocol beneficiary.
dop.recipients.v1.method: Decode the (address, share) array emitted at launch and count distinct addresses. The protocol beneficiary is identified by appearing on essentially every launch rather than by hardcoding it, so a redeployment does not silently corrupt the count.
excludes: Doppler's protocol beneficiary, present on every launch by construction.
Launches whose migrator path emits no split event.
does_not_assert: That a recipient is an agent, a company, or a person. It is an address that stands to receive fees.
That the recipient controls the token or the launch. It is the address the split names.

dop.launches.total.v1.title: Doppler token launches indexed
dop.launches.total.v1.definition: Distinct tokens created through the Doppler Airlock launch controller, counted from its Create event.
dop.launches.total.v1.method: Sweep Airlock logs on the keyless Base RPC mesh in 9,999-block windows. The watermark never advances past a window that failed to read, so a gap is a stall rather than silent data loss.
excludes: Tokens launched by any other mechanism. This is one launch layer, not the whole of Base.
does_not_assert: That these are agent tokens. Doppler is general-purpose infrastructure; its documentation names Zora, Paragraph, Noice and Bankr among its integrators, and most launches will be neither agents nor businesses.

dop.smartaccount.rate30d.v1.title: Share of Doppler token launches signed by a smart account
dop.smartaccount.rate30d.v1.definition: Of the Airlock launches in the last 30 days whose signing route we have classified, the share whose transaction was sent to an ERC-4337 EntryPoint or the Doppler Bundler rather than being a direct call from an externally owned account.
dop.smartaccount.rate30d.v1.method: Read the top-level `to` of each launch transaction. EntryPoint v0.6 and v0.7 both count as account abstraction; counting only v0.7 understates the share by about nine points.
excludes: Launches whose route we have not classified yet. Classification costs one transaction fetch each and is filled in progressively; the denominator is always the number actually classified, published beside it as doppler_launches_route_classified_30d.
does_not_assert: That a smart-account launch was made by an autonomous agent. A smart account is a contract wallet, and a person can sign through one; this measures the wallet type, not who decided.
Anything about which front-end drove the launch. Airlock records the integrator in a mapping rather than an event, so it is not recoverable from logs.

That the rate is stable over Doppler's life. It is not — the oldest blocks we swept run about 29 EOA launches to every 1 smart-account launch, which is why this is windowed at 30 days rather than measured all-time.

dop.oneshot.rate.v1.title: Share of Doppler fee recipients that appear exactly once
dop.oneshot.rate.v1.definition: External fee-recipient addresses named in exactly one launch split, divided by all external fee recipients.
dop.oneshot.rate.v1.method: Group the beneficiary table by address, excluding Doppler's own protocol beneficiary, and count those with a single launch.
excludes: Doppler's protocol beneficiary, which is present on every launch by construction.
does_not_assert: That a one-launch recipient is inactive or abandoned. It has launched once so far, which is the ordinary case.

dop.launches.30d.v1.title: Doppler token launches in the last 30 days
dop.launches.30d.v1.definition: Airlock Create events with a block timestamp inside the last 30 days.
dop.launches.30d.v1.method: Counted from the indexed launch table. Published ONLY once the sweep has reached the chain head — mid-backfill this counts how far we have read rather than what happened, so it is withheld instead.
excludes: Everything outside the window, and everything in blocks not yet swept.
does_not_assert: That launch volume is demand. A launch is a contract deployment; most of these tokens will never trade meaningfully.

dop.smartaccount.ratelife.v1.title: Share of all classified Doppler launches signed by a smart account
dop.smartaccount.ratelife.v1.definition: The same measure as the 30-day rate, computed over every launch we have classified regardless of age.
dop.smartaccount.ratelife.v1.method: Read the top-level `to` of each launch transaction; both ERC-4337 EntryPoint versions count as account abstraction.
excludes: Launches not yet classified.
does_not_assert: That this figure describes the layer today. It deliberately mixes eras — early Airlock launches run about 29 EOA to every 1 smart account, recent ones the other way — and is published only so the shift is visible beside the windowed number. Use the 30-day rate for anything current.

dop.routed30d.v1.title: Recent Doppler launches whose signing route is classified
dop.routed30d.v1.definition: Launches in the last 30 days for which we have fetched the transaction and recorded how it was signed.
dop.routed30d.v1.method: One transaction fetch per launch, filled in progressively newest-first rather than all at once.
excludes: Launches not yet classified.
does_not_assert: That the classified set is a random sample. It is biased toward recent launches by construction, which is why it is only ever used as the denominator for a same-window rate.

drain.abandoned.v1.title: Drain, wallet abandoned (candidates)
drain.abandoned.v1.window: every dominant-share window in the ledger
drain.abandoned.v1.definition: A dominant-share window is opened when, in the 72 hours after an agent's first counted payment to a new payee, that payee takes at least 80% of everything the agent paid, the window's sum is at least five times the agent's previous largest payment and at least $250, after at least three earlier payments, with two or more payments of varying amounts. The window is a candidate when the payee is not a service (no label in our book, paid by fewer than ten registered agents) and the agent has made no counted payment to anyone else from the end of the 72 hours until now, with at least 30 days of that silence observed. Statuses: service, resumed (it paid others later), pending (silent, fewer than 30 days observed), candidate.
drain.abandoned.v1.method: The ledger only (counted payments: routing hops and pre-registration transfers excluded); no chain read. One fix on 13 October 2026 before publication: the first version asked for 30 silent days after the window and kept three agents that resumed paying later, which the 11 October human reading of the same 44 windows had marked ambiguous. With silence until now, the rule keeps no window the reading did not pick.
excludes: Payees with a label in our book or paid by ten or more registered agents.
Agents that paid anyone else after the window, at any time since.
does_not_assert: A theft. A person cashing out and a thief with a stolen key leave the same shape: a fresh address takes most of the money, then silence. Candidates are published for reading, never in the incident log, and the exit pack adds where the money went next.

erc8004.chain.base.v1.title: ERC-8004 registrations on Base
erc8004.chain.base.v1.definition: Registrations on Base, as reported by the cited census.
erc8004.chain.base.v1.method: Read from agenteconomy.to. Our own independent mint count for Base is published separately as registrations_minted_total; where they differ, both stand.
excludes: Other chains.
does_not_assert: That these are distinct operators, or live agents.

dq.checks.v1.title: Data-quality checks run
dq.checks.v1.definition: Number of assertion checks the data-quality suite ran over the tables every public number is computed from.
dq.checks.v1.method: Each check is a SQL query that returns zero rows when the data is healthy. The catalogue, severities and thresholds are published at /api/dq.
excludes: Checks that exist only as ideas; a check counts once it runs on the timer.
does_not_assert: That the data is correct in ways no check tests. A passing suite is evidence against known failure shapes, not proof of truth.

dq.passing.v1.title: Data-quality checks passing
dq.passing.v1.definition: Checks in the latest run that returned zero failing rows.
dq.passing.v1.method: Counted by the suite itself; informational checks that flag a known, expected shape (batch payments, shared operator wallets) count as not passing but never lower the health score.
does_not_assert: That a failing informational check is a defect.

dq.block.v1.title: Blocking data-quality failures
dq.block.v1.definition: Checks of severity block that failed: while one of these fails, some published number is wrong.
dq.block.v1.method: Examples: an agent ranked L7+ with no countable payment behind it, a payment counted from before the agent existed, a published rate outside 0–1.
does_not_assert: Which number is wrong; read the check and its sample at /api/dq.

dq.health.v1.title: Data-quality health score
dq.health.v1.definition: Weighted pass rate over block and warn checks.
dq.health.v1.method: Weight = dataset weight (tables the public rank is built from 3, published snapshots 2, partner tables 1) × severity (block 2, warn 1). Informational checks never move the score; a check that errors counts as failing.
excludes: Informational checks.
does_not_assert: Accuracy against the chain itself; it measures internal consistency and freshness.

erc8004.chain.bnb.v1.title: ERC-8004 registrations on BNB Smart Chain
erc8004.chain.bnb.v1.definition: Registrations on BNB Smart Chain, as reported by the cited census.
erc8004.chain.bnb.v1.method: Read from agenteconomy.to. Not reproduced — our own scans cover Base only.
excludes: Other chains.
does_not_assert: That these are distinct operators, or live agents. We have no independent measurement on this chain at all.

dq.warn.v1.title: Warning data-quality failures
dq.warn.v1.definition: Checks of severity warn that failed: something is late or drifting, but published numbers are still correct.
dq.warn.v1.method: Examples: a payment scan that has stalled, a promotion to L7 that has not happened yet.
does_not_assert: That a published number is wrong.

erc8004.chain.eth.v1.title: ERC-8004 registrations on Ethereum
erc8004.chain.eth.v1.definition: Registrations on Ethereum mainnet, as reported by the cited census.
erc8004.chain.eth.v1.method: Read from agenteconomy.to. Not reproduced — our own scans cover Base only.
excludes: Other chains.
does_not_assert: That these are distinct operators, or live agents. We have no independent measurement on this chain.
