erc8004.protocol.declared.v1.title: Share of registrations declaring a protocol
erc8004.protocol.declared.v1.definition: Share of registrations that name a protocol or capability in their record, as reported by the census source.
erc8004.protocol.declared.v1.method: Read from the cited census. Not reproduced.
does_not_assert: That a declared protocol is implemented.

eth.out.checked.v1.title: Paying agent wallets read for native ETH
eth.out.checked.v1.definition: Bound wallets of L7+ agents whose native ETH sends have been read up to the latest run. Smart-contract wallets and keys that never sent a transaction count as read. The coverage behind eth.out.wallets.30d.v1 and eth.out.usd.30d.v1.

eth.out.usd.30d.v1.title: Native ETH sent by paying agent wallets, last 30 days (USD)
eth.out.usd.30d.v1.window: sends in the last 30 days; read every 6 hours
eth.out.usd.30d.v1.definition: USD value of the native ETH counted in eth.out.wallets.30d.v1, each send priced at the hour it was sent.
eth.out.usd.30d.v1.method: As eth.out.wallets.30d.v1. Each send is priced with our own ETH/USD series (CoinGecko) at the nearest earlier hour, or the latest price if the series has no point in the 72 hours before it.
excludes: As eth.out.wallets.30d.v1.
Not part of counted spending (pay.usd.total.v1), which stays the four stablecoins until a dated method change says otherwise.
does_not_assert: That the ETH was spending.

erc8004.declares.wallet.v1.title: Share of registrations declaring an agent wallet
erc8004.declares.wallet.v1.definition: Share of probed registrations whose descriptor names a wallet address the agent claims to control.
erc8004.declares.wallet.v1.method: Read the parsed descriptor for a declared address. This is the join that makes everything downstream possible: without a declared wallet there is nothing to watch.
excludes: Registrations whose descriptor did not parse.
does_not_assert: That the agent controls the declared wallet. A declaration is a claim, and a claim is not a binding — which is why the binding record spec exists and why a declared wallet alone never raises an agent above L5.

erc8004.registrations.scan8004.v1.title: ERC-8004 registrations, per 8004scan
erc8004.registrations.scan8004.v1.method: Read from their public interface. Not reproduced by us.
excludes: Whatever chains they do not index.
does_not_assert: That this is the number of agents. It is the number of rows minted in a registry, and anyone can mint one.
That it agrees with the other census. It does not, by roughly an order of magnitude, and we publish both rather than choosing.

erc8004.source.gap.v1.title: Disagreement between the two registration counts
erc8004.source.gap.v1.definition: The difference between the two independent registration censuses.
erc8004.source.gap.v1.method: Subtraction. Published deliberately: two sources counting the same registry and differing by this much is the single most useful caveat on any 'how many agents are there' claim.
does_not_assert: That one source is wrong. They count different chain sets and different inclusion rules, and neither publishes enough for us to adjudicate.
That the true figure lies between them.

erc8004.registrations.agenteconomy.v1.title: ERC-8004 registrations, per agenteconomy.to
erc8004.registrations.agenteconomy.v1.definition: The registration count published by agenteconomy.to.
erc8004.registrations.agenteconomy.v1.method: Read from their public interface. Not reproduced by us.
excludes: Whatever chains they do not index.
does_not_assert: That this is the number of agents.

That it agrees with 8004scan. The gap between the two is published as its own number, because a disagreement between sources is a fact about the sector rather than something to hide behind whichever figure we preferred.

eth.out.wallets.30d.v1.title: Paying agent wallets that sent native ETH, last 30 days
eth.out.wallets.30d.v1.window: sends in the last 30 days; read every 6 hours
eth.out.wallets.30d.v1.definition: Distinct bound wallets of agents ranked L7 or above that sent native ETH to another address in the last 30 days, in a transaction the wallet itself signed.
eth.out.wallets.30d.v1.method: alchemy_getAssetTransfers (category external, fromAddress = the bound wallet). A wallet is read again only when its transaction count has moved since the last run (read from Base's public node), and the first read reaches back 30 days. A smart-contract wallet cannot sign a transaction, so it never sends ETH this way; it is covered without a read. EIP-7702-delegated keys still sign and are read. The figure is published only once the read covers 95% of the wallets.
excludes: ETH a smart-contract wallet sends through an internal call (Alchemy does not serve internal transfers on Base).
WETH, which is an ERC-20.
Sends from a wallet to itself.
does_not_assert: That the ETH was spending. It can be gas top-ups for other wallets, transfers between one operator's own wallets, or a drain.

fleet.sibling.v1.title: fleet_sibling_exposure: a drained agent's operator set
fleet.sibling.v1.window: drain-shaped incidents of the last 30 days
fleet.sibling.v1.definition: For each drain_pattern or test_then_drain incident, one info-severity notice on every other registration in the same operator set (cluster.ratio.v1: same bound wallet, same current owner, same minter or same first funder, each link ignored above 50 registrations), at most 100 per drain, naming the drained sibling and the links. Shared frailty (Cui 2022, Example 14): one failure in a cluster raises the predicted risk of the rest; an operator watching any of them hears about it.
fleet.sibling.v1.method: afg-incidents, hourly, from lib/clusters.mjs. Never a live incident and never an alert to the public channel; delivered to chats and desks that watch the sibling.
excludes: Registrations whose only link to the drained agent is a platform-level one (an owner, minter or funder above 50 registrations).
does_not_assert: That the sibling is at risk, or that one person controls the set: the registrations share a chain fact, and the drain on one of them is a shape, not a verdict.

graph.bound.wallets.v1.title: Bound wallets sampled
graph.bound.wallets.v1.definition: How many agent-declared wallets the balance sweep read in this pass.
graph.bound.wallets.v1.method: An even sample across Base registrations rather than the newest or the richest.
excludes: Wallets outside the sample, and registrations that declare no wallet.
does_not_assert: That the sample is the whole population. Rates computed from it are estimates with a stated denominator.

graph.funded.rate.v1.title: Share of bound wallets that hold money
graph.funded.rate.v1.definition: Funded bound wallets divided by bound wallets sampled.
graph.funded.rate.v1.method: Arithmetic on the two counts above, both from the same sweep so the denominator always matches the numerator.
excludes: The same exclusions as the two inputs.
does_not_assert: That the remainder are abandoned. It asserts that most declared agent wallets are empty at the moment we looked, which is a fact about readiness, not about intent.

fx.usdc.v1.title: USDC price in US dollars
fx.usdc.v1.definition: The market price of one USDC.
does_not_assert: That USDC is worth a dollar. It is published precisely so a depeg would be visible rather than assumed away — every USD figure we compute from USDC amounts inherits this number.

graph.funded.wallets.v1.title: Bound wallets holding money
graph.funded.wallets.v1.definition: How many of the sampled bound wallets hold at least one dollar of USDC on Base.
excludes: Balances in other assets and on other chains. A wallet funded entirely in ETH, or on another chain, counts as unfunded here.
does_not_assert: That an unfunded wallet is a dead agent. It may be funded just in time, or hold value we do not look at. It does mean the agent cannot pay from this address right now.

graph.bound.usdc.v1.title: Total USDC across sampled bound wallets
graph.bound.usdc.v1.definition: The summed USDC balance of every bound wallet in the sample.
graph.bound.usdc.v1.method: Balance reads, summed. USD conversion uses the published USDC price rather than an assumed dollar.
excludes: Other assets, other chains, and wallets outside the sample.
does_not_assert: That this is the agent economy's cash. It is a sample total, and the median beside it exists because a handful of wallets dominate the sum.

graph.bound.usdc.median.v1.title: Median USDC in a funded bound wallet
graph.bound.usdc.median.v1.definition: The median balance among sampled bound wallets that hold USDC.
graph.bound.usdc.median.v1.method: Median rather than mean, over funded wallets only.
excludes: Empty wallets, which would drag the median to zero and describe nothing.
does_not_assert: That a typical agent holds this. It is the middle of the funded ones, which are a minority.

graph.objects.actors.v1.title: Actors in the graph
graph.objects.actors.v1.definition: Actor rows we hold — every registration we have sampled and joined, at any rung of the ladder.
excludes: Registrations we have never sampled.
does_not_assert: That these are live agents. Most sit at the bottom of the ladder; the rung counts are published separately.

graph.objects.wallets.v1.title: Wallets in the graph
graph.objects.wallets.v1.definition: Distinct wallet addresses we hold a record for.
excludes: Addresses we have never seen declared or paid.
does_not_assert: That each wallet belongs to a distinct party.

graph.series.points.v1.title: Time-series observations stored
graph.series.points.v1.definition: How many time-series observations the collector holds.
graph.series.points.v1.method: Counted from our own store. The archive published to the site is a downsample of this; the full resolution stays with our collector.
does_not_assert: That every point is published. The public file keeps one point per day plus a 48-hour five-minute tail.

graph.objects.bindings.v1.title: Open actor-to-wallet bindings
graph.objects.bindings.v1.definition: Currently open bindings joining an actor to a wallet.
graph.objects.bindings.v1.method: Counted from our own store. Closed bindings are retained as an audit trail and excluded here, so this is a present-tense count rather than a running total.
excludes: Closed bindings.
does_not_assert: That a binding proves control. It records the evidence we hold for the join; the strength of that evidence is what the ladder grades.

idle.actors.v1.title: Funded agents that have not paid anyone
idle.actors.v1.definition: Agents whose bound wallet holds at least $10 of USDC and which have made no countable payment to any counterparty in the last 7 days.
idle.actors.v1.method: Latest balance read per bound wallet, against the most recent countable PAY per actor.
excludes: Agents with no balance read yet — absence of a reading is not evidence of an empty wallet.
does_not_assert: That the agent is broken or abandoned. A week of not paying is a week of not paying; some jobs are monthly.
That the balance is intended to be spent at all.

graph.objects.probes.v1.title: Endpoint probe results recorded
graph.objects.probes.v1.definition: Every endpoint probe result we have stored.
graph.objects.probes.v1.method: Counted from our own store. Failures are kept, not overwritten — a probe history is how the dead-endpoint detector works.
does_not_assert: That each probe is a distinct agent. One agent is probed repeatedly over time.

idle.usd.v1.title: USDC held by idle funded agents
idle.usd.v1.definition: Total USDC held by agents with at least $10 that have not paid anyone in seven days.
idle.usd.v1.method: Balance of bound wallets joined against last observed payment. Both thresholds are stated choices, published so they can be argued with.
excludes: Agents below the balance threshold, and activity we cannot observe — an agent paying on another chain looks idle here.
does_not_assert: That the money is stranded or abandoned. It asserts that money is sitting next to an agent without moving, which is the gap between an agent economy existing and an agent economy running.

graph.objects.money.v1.title: Payment rows recorded
graph.objects.money.v1.definition: Every payment row we hold, including those excluded from published totals.
graph.objects.money.v1.method: Counted from our own store. Deliberately larger than the published payment count: rows dated before their agent's registration are kept and flagged rather than deleted, so the exclusion is auditable.
does_not_assert: That every row counts toward observed volume. Roughly a quarter do not, and the excluded value is published as its own figure.

incident.live.v2.title: Live incidents
incident.live.v2.definition: Detections that are a harm AND recent: a retry loop burning an agent's money, a registration changing owner under a binding somebody relies on, or signing delegated to an implementation outside the curated allowlist, with an event time inside the last 72 hours.
incident.live.v2.method: Each hourly detector run closes any row that is not a harm kind or has aged out of the window, so the open flag means exactly this rule and nothing else. Mint bursts are never incidents.
excludes: Mint bursts, of any size. They measure a shape, not a harm.
Endpoints that never answer. That is a statement about our attempts, not damage done to anyone.
Anything older than 72 hours, which stays in the detection log.
does_not_assert: That zero means nothing bad is happening anywhere. It means none of these detectors has fired on a harm in what we measure.
That an incident is malicious. An identity changing owner can be a legitimate sale; it is an incident because anyone relying on the old owner is now exposed.

incident.open.v1.title: Open incidents
incident.open.v1.definition: Recorded events found by our detectors that remain open.
incident.open.v1.method: Queries over our own measurements. No external calls.
excludes: States. A low liveness score is a measurement, not an incident, and never appears here.
does_not_assert: That an incident is wrongdoing. A bulk minting burst is legitimate behaviour that changes what a registration count means.

income.actors.30d.v1.title: Agents with income, 30 days
income.actors.30d.v1.definition: Ranked agents with a counted income transfer dated in the last 30 days.
income.actors.30d.v1.method: Distinct actor over money_events of kind EARN in the window.
excludes: Agents whose wallets the income scan has not read yet.
does_not_assert: That the agent earned the money.

income.actors.v1.title: Agents with income
income.actors.v1.definition: Ranked agents with at least one counted income transfer.
income.actors.v1.method: Distinct actor over money_events of kind EARN.
excludes: Agents whose wallets the income scan has not read yet.
does_not_assert: That the agent earned the money.

income.events.v1.title: Income transfers
income.events.v1.window: all time since each registration's mint block
income.events.v1.definition: Counted stablecoin transfers into ranked agents (income.usd.total.v1 rules).
income.events.v1.method: Count over money_events of kind EARN.
excludes: Everything income.usd.total.v1 excludes.
does_not_assert: That each transfer is a sale.

income.netflow.30d.v1.title: Net flow, 30 days
income.netflow.30d.v1.definition: Agent income over the window (income.usd.total.v1 rules) minus counted agent spending over the window (pay.usd.total.v1 rules).
income.netflow.30d.v1.method: Two sums over money_events, kinds EARN and PAY, same exclusions.
excludes: Everything either side excludes.
does_not_assert: Profitability. Income includes operator top-ups; spending includes purchases the operator intended.

income.payers.v1.title: Addresses that paid agents
income.payers.v1.definition: Distinct senders of counted income transfers into ranked agents.
income.payers.v1.method: Distinct from-address over money_events of kind EARN.
does_not_assert: That a payer is a customer. An operator funding its own agent is a payer here.

income.usd.30d.v1.title: Agent income, 30 days
income.usd.30d.v1.definition: Agent income (income.usd.total.v1 rules) dated in the last 30 days.
income.usd.30d.v1.method: Sum over money_events of kind EARN, same exclusions.
excludes: Everything income.usd.total.v1 excludes.
does_not_assert: That the money paid for work rather than funding the agent.

partner.7702.delegated.v1.title: Delegated bound agent wallets
partner.7702.delegated.v1.definition: Bound wallets whose on-chain code is the EIP-7702 designator followed by an implementation address.
partner.7702.delegated.v1.method: Read exactly from the wallet's code. Nothing else produces that byte pattern.
excludes: Wallets whose code we have not read.
does_not_assert: Risk. Delegation is the intended mechanism, not a defect.

ladder.transition.v1.title: Day-to-day moves between L7, L8, L9 and out
ladder.transition.v1.unit: agent-days per move, and the share of each row
ladder.transition.v1.definition: Each day, the level of every ranked agent is recorded; the matrix counts, for every pair of consecutive days, how many agents moved from each level to each level, or out of the rank. A measured transition matrix, not a reconstruction.
ladder.transition.v1.method: afg-ladderdyn, daily, from actors.liveness at run time. The first move can be counted on the second day; the document says how many snapshot days it holds.
excludes: Levels below L7 (not ranked).
does_not_assert: That a move out of the rank is an exit of any kind: it can be a withdrawn binding or a payment reclassified.

market.move.2sigma.v1.title: Anomalous daily move
market.move.2sigma.v1.window: 30 complete days of trailing baseline, minimum 20 observations
market.move.2sigma.v1.definition: A metric whose latest complete-day observation lies at least two standard deviations from the mean of its own trailing baseline, AND whose move clears a per-metric absolute floor.
market.move.2sigma.v1.method: The statistic depends on how the metric moves: a cumulative counter is differenced to a daily increment, a level becomes a day-over-day percentage change, a rate becomes a percentage-point change, and a daily flow is used as-is. Guessing a family would be worse than silence, so a metric with no declared family is never tested.
excludes: The current UTC day, always — a partial day against a full-day baseline is a different measurement, not a small error.
Metrics with fewer than 20 baseline observations.
does_not_assert: Causation, or that the move is news. It says the number is unusual for itself, which is the only thing statistics can say.
That an unflagged day was uneventful — a move can be real and still sit inside two sigma of a volatile series.

income.usd.total.v1.title: Agent income
income.usd.total.v1.window: all time since each registration's mint block
income.usd.total.v1.definition: The summed USD value of stablecoin transfers INTO a wallet bound to a ranked registration (USDC, USDT, EURC at the day's rate, DAI), from a different address, after the registration existed.
income.usd.total.v1.method: alchemy_getAssetTransfers with toAddress over every ranked wallet, each re-read about twice a week; the same receipt check as spending marks money that arrived and left in one transaction as a hop.
excludes: Transfers dated before the registration's mint block.
Money that left again in the same transaction (a hop or a swap).
Self-transfers.
Wallets not yet read: the count is a floor while the first pass runs.
does_not_assert: That the transfer paid for the agent's work rather than funding it: an operator topping up a wallet is income here too. Payers that are themselves ranked agents are the closest thing to earned revenue, and are separable by address.

issuer.freeze.v1.title: Issuer freezes on Base
issuer.freeze.v1.definition: The stablecoin issuers' own freeze and unfreeze events, read from the chain: Circle's Blacklisted and UnBlacklisted on USDC and EURC, Tether's AddedBlackList and RemovedBlackList on USDT. An address is frozen for a token when its latest event on that token is a freeze. Beside the set: which addresses that registered agents paid in counted payments are frozen, and which bound agent wallets are.
issuer.freeze.v1.method: afg-freezes, hourly, eth_getLogs on the three token contracts with a cursor. The label source StableAML (Juvinski et al. 2026) found decisive: a frozen address cannot move the token at all.
excludes: Other chains, other tokens, and any list that is not the issuer's own on-chain act.
does_not_assert: Why the issuer froze an address, or anything about the person behind it: the fact is the issuer's.

ladder.exit_incidence.v1.title: How ranked agents end: cumulative incidence per cause
ladder.exit_incidence.v1.unit: share (0-1) at 30, 60, 90 and 180 days, with the number at risk
ladder.exit_incidence.v1.window: from each agent's first payment that left its control, to today
ladder.exit_incidence.v1.definition: For every ranked agent, time is counted from its first payment that left its control (rank.l7plus.v2) until the first of four competing exits: drained (a drain_pattern or test_then_drain incident on it), abandoned (a drain.abandoned.v1 candidate window, dated at the window's end), dormant (no counted payment for 30 days, dated at the last payment plus 30 days), or none yet (censored today). The cumulative incidence of each cause is the Aalen-Johansen estimator (1 minus Kaplan-Meier per cause overstates it); no_exit is the Kaplan-Meier probability of no exit; rmst is the restricted mean time without an exit over the first 90 days.
ladder.exit_incidence.v1.method: afg-ladderdyn, daily at 03:40 UTC, queries only over money_events, incidents and the exit-window rule. Numbers at risk are printed under every horizon.
excludes: Bridged-away as an exit (not measured yet).
Agents whose payments never left their control (not ranked).
does_not_assert: That drained means stolen (a shape), or that dormant means dead: an agent ends its silence with one payment.
Anything about agents below L7.

partner.7702.allowlisted.v1.title: Share of delegated agent wallets on an allowlisted implementation
partner.7702.allowlisted.v1.definition: Delegated bound wallets pointing at an implementation on our published allowlist, divided by all delegated bound wallets.
partner.7702.allowlisted.v1.method: Read the 7702 designator from each wallet's code and match the implementation address against the allowlist file.
excludes: Wallets whose code we have not read.
does_not_assert: That non-allowlisted implementations are malicious. The allowlist ships EMPTY on purpose: an implementation nobody has read is unknown rather than untrusted, so this figure reads zero by design until somebody does the reading.
Safety. An allowlisted implementation can still be used badly.

partner.7702.eoa.v1.title: Visible externally-owned bound wallets
partner.7702.eoa.v1.definition: Bound wallets we have examined that carry no code at all.
partner.7702.eoa.v1.method: Counted only over wallets whose code we have actually read.
excludes: Wallets never examined.
does_not_assert: That these wallets are unsafe. It asserts that whatever policy governs them is not enforced on-chain, which is a different and narrower statement.

partner.7702.unknown.v1.title: Share of delegated agent wallets on an unrecognised implementation
partner.7702.unknown.v1.method: Derived from the same single query, so the two cannot disagree.
excludes: Wallets whose code we have not read.
does_not_assert: That the implementations are dangerous. Unknown means unread, and reading them is work nobody has published.

partner.fetch.attempted.v1.title: Fetch / Almanac identities attempted
partner.fetch.attempted.v1.definition: Almanac identities we have ingested from the Agentverse search API and run our qualifier against.
partner.fetch.attempted.v1.method: The search index caps any single query at 10,000 results, so we rotate a term list and page through each. Every row records which term produced it.
excludes: Almanac rows we have not reached yet. This is our attempted set, not their registry.
does_not_assert: That this is the size of the Almanac. It is the size of what we have checked, which is the only denominator a reader can reproduce.
That the sample is uniform. The term list is deliberately weighted toward money — wallet, usdc, x402, treasury — which biases the bind rate UPWARD. A uniform sample would return a lower figure.

partner.circle.l7float.v1.title: USDC float on wallets we have watched pay
partner.circle.l7float.v1.definition: USDC held across wallets bound to an actor at liveness 7 or above.
partner.circle.l7float.v1.method: Balances read on the keyless public mesh through Multicall3, batched 50 wallets per call.
excludes: Wallets we have not bound, and every asset other than USDC on Base.
does_not_assert: USDC held by agents in general. It is a floor over the agents WE bound and observed, and the true figure is larger by an unknown amount.
That this money is destined to be spent. It is float, which is the point of measuring it separately from payments.

partner.7702.topfloat.v1.title: Float share of the top 7702 implementation
partner.7702.topfloat.v1.definition: USDC held by delegated bound wallets pointing at the single most common implementation, divided by USDC held by all delegated bound wallets.
partner.7702.topfloat.v1.method: Weighted by float rather than by wallet count, because blast radius is money and not headcount.
excludes: Wallets whose code we have not read, and assets other than USDC.
does_not_assert: That the implementation is at risk. It says how much money would be affected if it were.
That a wallet-count share would look the same. It usually does not: ten dust wallets are not one funded one.

partner.fetch.moved.v1.title: Fetch / Almanac wallets that moved USDC
partner.fetch.moved.v1.definition: Bound Almanac wallets observed sending USDC to a different address after the identity existed.
partner.fetch.moved.v1.method: Same asset-transfer read as every other catalog. Self-transfers and burn addresses excluded.
excludes: Self-transfers.
Fetch-chain activity.
does_not_assert: L7. See partner.virtuals.moved.v1 for why an outbound transfer is not a payment for work.

partner.fetch.bound.v1.title: Fetch / Almanac identities bound to a payable wallet
partner.fetch.bound.v1.definition: Attempted Almanac identities for which we found an EVM address in the agent card, and which do not share that address with another identity in the same catalog.
partner.fetch.bound.v1.method: Scan the agent card for an EVM address, excluding burn addresses. An Almanac identity is itself a Fetch-chain bech32 address and cannot receive USDC on Base.
excludes: Fetch-chain addresses, which are a different money object.
Identities sharing a declared wallet with another identity.
does_not_assert: That unbound agents are fake or inactive. It asserts only that nothing in their card tells us where to pay them on Base.
That Fetch-native spending does not exist. It does, and it would be published as its own series rather than folded into a Base figure.

partner.fetch.bind_rate.v1.title: Fetch / Almanac bind rate
partner.fetch.bind_rate.v1.definition: Bound identities divided by attempted identities.
partner.fetch.bind_rate.v1.method: One query, so both counts come from the same instant. Reading a numerator and a denominator from separate queries during an active ingest once published a negative ratio.
excludes: Identities we have not attempted.
does_not_assert: A ceiling on how many Almanac agents handle money. It is a floor on how many we could pay, which is a narrower claim.
That the rate is unbiased. Our sampling deliberately favours money-related agents, so this figure is an upper bound.

partner.fetch.theiractive.v1.title: Almanac identities Agentverse itself marks active, in our sample
partner.fetch.theiractive.v1.definition: Identities in our ingested Fetch sample whose Agentverse status is active — their reachability object, counted on our rows.
partner.fetch.theiractive.v1.method: Read from their own status field. Published beside our bind rate so the two objects sit on the same sample.
excludes: Almanac rows we have not ingested.
does_not_assert: Our L5. Their active means reachable and unexpired on their infrastructure; ours means an endpoint answered our probe. The two are allowed to disagree and are never merged.
A judgement about their registry. It is their number, on our sample, so a reader can see both objects at once.

partner.virtuals.attempted.v1.title: Virtuals identities attempted
partner.virtuals.attempted.v1.definition: Virtuals agent identities we have ingested from the public catalog API and run our qualifier against.
partner.virtuals.attempted.v1.method: Paged through the public catalog, a few hundred per run, advancing a cursor so the set grows visibly over days rather than arriving as one unverifiable dump.
excludes: Catalog rows we have not reached yet.
does_not_assert: That this is the size of the Virtuals catalog. It is the size of what we have checked.

partner.virtuals.bind_rate.v1.title: Virtuals bind rate
partner.virtuals.bind_rate.v1.definition: Bound identities divided by attempted identities.
partner.virtuals.bind_rate.v1.method: One query, so numerator and denominator come from the same instant.
excludes: Identities we have not attempted.
Identities on a shared wallet, which are excluded from the numerator.
does_not_assert: That a bound agent is a live agent. Binding is a join and nothing more.

partner.virtuals.jobrail.v1.title: Virtuals identities carrying an ACP identity
partner.virtuals.jobrail.v1.definition: Identities in our ingested set that declare an Agent Commerce Protocol agent id — registration on the job rail.
partner.virtuals.jobrail.v1.method: Presence of acpAgentId or v3AcpAgentId in the catalog record.
excludes: Identities with a token address but no ACP id, counted separately.
does_not_assert: That a job was sold, requested, evaluated or settled. It is a registration on a job protocol, not a transaction on one — we do not ingest ACP job state yet.
That the agent is live. An ACP id is a name on a second rail, and a name is not a worker.

partner.virtuals.hastoken.v1.title: Virtuals identities carrying a token address
partner.virtuals.hastoken.v1.definition: Identities in our ingested set with a deployed token address — registration on the token rail.
partner.virtuals.hastoken.v1.method: Presence of tokenAddress in the catalog record. Recorded as an attribute and NEVER used as a binding.
excludes: Pre-launch identities, which have no token yet.
does_not_assert: Value, revenue or capital at work. A token address is a contract, and its holders are fans rather than operators.
That the agent can be paid. The token address is not a wallet and we never bind to one.

partner.virtuals.l7_rate_q.v1.title: Virtuals moved-USDC rate, alternate id
partner.virtuals.l7_rate_q.v1.definition: Retained identifier for the moved-USDC rate over wallets read, kept so that series rows written before the metric was renamed still resolve.
partner.virtuals.l7_rate_q.v1.method: Superseded by partner.virtuals.moved_rate.v1. The figure is identical; only the name changed, because the old one implied an L7 claim the measurement does not support.
excludes: Nothing additional.
does_not_assert: L7, despite the identifier. The rename exists precisely because the original name over-claimed.

partner.virtuals.maxop.v1.title: Most Virtuals identities from one operator
partner.virtuals.maxop.v1.definition: The largest number of ingested identities sharing a single creator account id.
partner.virtuals.maxop.v1.method: Group by the catalog's own creator account id and take the maximum.
excludes: Rows with no operator key yet, which is why this figure only rises.
does_not_assert: Wrongdoing. A prolific creator is a prolific creator.
A final value. It grows as coverage grows, which is why it is a live figure rather than a sentence.

partner.virtuals.bound.v1.title: Virtuals identities bound to a sole-declarant wallet
partner.virtuals.bound.v1.definition: Attempted Virtuals identities declaring an agent wallet, or an ERC-6551 token-bound account where no agent wallet is declared, which no other identity in the same catalog also declares.
partner.virtuals.bound.v1.method: Take the declared agent wallet first, then the token-bound account. The token address is recorded as an attribute and never bound.
excludes: Token addresses. Holders are fans, not operators.
Identities sharing a wallet with another identity in the same catalog — one address in this catalog is declared by 84 different agents.
does_not_assert: That each bound identity is a distinct operator. Same-funder clustering across DISTINCT wallets is not applied yet, so read this as an upper bound.
That a bound wallet has done anything. Binding is a join, not evidence of activity.

partner.virtuals.available.v1.title: Virtuals identities their catalog marks launched
partner.virtuals.available.v1.definition: Identities in our ingested set whose status in the Virtuals catalog is AVAILABLE — launched and tradeable.
partner.virtuals.available.v1.method: Read from their own status field on our own rows. Their object, counted on our sample.
excludes: Identities we have not ingested.
does_not_assert: That a launched agent is a working agent. Launch is a token event.
Our own liveness. This is their status field, published beside ours so a reader can see the two are answers to different questions.

partner.virtuals.qualified.v1.title: Virtuals bound wallets read on-chain
partner.virtuals.qualified.v1.definition: Bound Virtuals wallets whose transfer history we have actually read.
partner.virtuals.qualified.v1.method: Capped per run and paced against the provider budget, oldest check first.
excludes: Bound wallets still queued for a read.
does_not_assert: That unread wallets are inactive. They are unread, and every rate we publish over this set says so.

partner.virtuals.maxshare.v1.title: Most Virtuals identities declaring one single wallet
partner.virtuals.maxshare.v1.definition: The largest number of Virtuals identities in our ingested set that declare the same wallet address.
partner.virtuals.maxshare.v1.method: Group declarations by address within the partner's own catalog and take the maximum.
excludes: Identities we have not ingested yet, which is why this figure only ever rises.
does_not_assert: Wrongdoing. Launching many agents from one wallet is ordinary; this measures a naming habit, not a deception.

A final value. It was 84 when first measured on a small sample and grows as we read further into the catalog, which is exactly why it is published as a live figure rather than written into a sentence.

partner.virtuals.operators.v1.title: Distinct operators behind Virtuals identities
partner.virtuals.operators.v1.definition: Distinct creator account ids across the ingested identities where the catalog supplies one.
partner.virtuals.operators.v1.method: The platform's own creator account id — an exact same-operator key, not an inference from funding patterns. ONLY the opaque integer is stored: the catalog returns an email address, a username and social handles beside it, and none of those enter this graph.
excludes: Rows ingested before 2026-09-12, when we began recording the key. Those backfill as the cursor cycles.
does_not_assert: That this is the number of operators on the platform. It is the number among rows where WE know the key — published beside `operator_known` so the coverage is never hidden.
That one operator running many agents is improper. It is ordinary, and it is the reason a name count and an actor count diverge.

partner.virtuals.perop.v1.title: Identities per operator
partner.virtuals.perop.v1.definition: Rows with a known creator account, divided by the distinct creator accounts among them.
partner.virtuals.perop.v1.method: Computed only over rows where the operator is known, so a partially backfilled set cannot flatter it.
excludes: Rows with no operator key yet.
does_not_assert: A catalog-wide ratio, until coverage approaches the full set. Read it against `operator_known` — both are published in the same block for that reason.
That the identities are duplicates. They are distinct agents; they share a person.

partner.virtuals.shared.v1.title: Virtuals shared-wallet rate
partner.virtuals.shared.v1.definition: The share of Virtuals identities declaring a wallet that at least one other identity in the same catalog also declares.
partner.virtuals.shared.v1.method: Group declarations by address within the partner's own catalog; any address with more than one declarant marks all of them.
excludes: Identities that declare no wallet at all.
does_not_assert: Wrongdoing. Launching many agents from one wallet is ordinary, and this measures a naming habit rather than a deception.
That the identities are related to each other in any other way. It says only that several names point at one address.

partner.virtuals.moved_rate.v1.title: Virtuals moved-USDC rate over wallets read
partner.virtuals.moved_rate.v1.definition: Wallets that moved USDC after launch, divided by the bound wallets we have actually read on-chain.
partner.virtuals.moved_rate.v1.method: Denominator is wallets READ, not wallets bound. While a sweep is working through a catalog of tens of thousands, a rate over the bound set would mostly measure how far the sweep has got.
excludes: Bound wallets not yet read.
does_not_assert: A liveness rate. See partner.virtuals.moved.v1 for what this counts and what it refuses to claim.

partner.virtuals.moved.v1.title: Virtuals wallets that moved USDC after launch
partner.virtuals.moved.v1.definition: Bound Virtuals wallets observed sending USDC to a DIFFERENT address at or after the identity's own launch date.
partner.virtuals.moved.v1.method: One asset-transfer read per wallet, capped per run. Self-transfers and burn addresses are excluded; transfers timestamped before the identity's launch are excluded and counted separately.
excludes: Self-transfers — moving your own money between your own wallets is not paying anybody.
Everything the wallet did before the agent existed. A declared wallet is frequently years older than the agent declared on it.
does_not_assert: L7. This is deliberately NOT our liveness rung. From a raw wallet read, a token launch, a bonding-curve buy, a liquidity add and a DEX swap are all outbound USDC transfers, and we cannot yet separate them from a payment for work.
That the counterparty was another agent, or that any service was delivered.

partner.virtuals.prelaunch.v1.title: Virtuals wallets with USDC history predating their agent
partner.virtuals.prelaunch.v1.definition: Bound Virtuals wallets whose observed outbound USDC transfers include at least one timestamped BEFORE the identity's own launch date.
partner.virtuals.prelaunch.v1.method: Compare each transfer's block timestamp against the identity's launch or creation date from the catalog.
excludes: Wallets whose entire history postdates their agent.
does_not_assert: Deception. People declare wallets they already had, which is ordinary.
That the pre-launch money was an agent's. It was a person's, which is exactly why it is excluded from every other figure — counting it once overstated our own published headline by 46%.

partner.x402.payers.v1.title: x402 payers we observe
partner.x402.payers.v1.definition: Distinct bound wallets we have watched pay a known x402 recipient address.
partner.x402.payers.v1.method: Join our own verified payments against the harvested x402 recipient set.
excludes: x402 payers we have not bound to an identity, which is almost all of them.
does_not_assert: The number of x402 payers on Base. See partner.x402.coverage.v1 for how small a slice this is.

partner.x402.coverage.v1.title: Our coverage of the x402 rail
partner.x402.coverage.v1.definition: Distinct x402 payers we observe, divided by the unique-payer count a public x402 index reports for the same chain.
partner.x402.coverage.v1.method: Numerator is ours: bound wallets we watched pay a known x402 recipient. Denominator is somebody else's published figure, cited rather than reproduced.
excludes: x402 activity by payers we have not bound.
does_not_assert: That our payer classes describe the rail. They describe our slice, and this number exists to say how small that slice is.
That the two figures are the same object. Ours is cumulative over bound wallets; theirs is a 24-hour unique-payer count.

partner.x402.tickets.v1.title: x402 tickets we observe
partner.x402.tickets.v1.definition: Verified payments from bound wallets that landed on a known x402 recipient address.
partner.x402.tickets.v1.method: Counted alongside unique payers on purpose: farms retry, so a ticket share always looks worse than a payer share.
excludes: Payments to x402 recipients we have not harvested.
does_not_assert: Total x402 volume. This is our observed slice and it is a floor.

pay.builder.attribution.v1.title: Counted payments carrying an app's Builder Code
pay.builder.attribution.v1.window: all time; transactions are read once
pay.builder.attribution.v1.definition: Counted payments whose transaction carries an ERC-8021 Builder Code: a suffix appended to the calldata by the app, wallet or agent framework that built the transaction. Reported as the USD attributed, the number of distinct codes, and the largest code's share of attributed USD.
pay.builder.attribution.v1.method: The transaction input is read from the public Base RPC and its ERC-8021 suffix parsed (schema 0: ASCII codes). Codes are registered in the Base Builder Codes registry (0x000000BC7E6457e610fe52Dcc0ca5b3ce59C8E80).
excludes: Transactions not yet read (reported as pending in the note).
Suffixes in schemas other than 0, which are counted but not decoded.
does_not_assert: Who operates an app: a code names an app that attributed itself, and its registered metadata is usually private.
That payments without a code were not made through an app.

partner.x402.farm.v1.title: x402 payers in a same-minter cluster
partner.x402.farm.v1.definition: Observed x402 payers whose ERC-8004 registration was minted by an address that minted 25 or more registrations.
partner.x402.farm.v1.method: Join the payer's registration to the registry's own mint records and group by minter.
excludes: Payers with no ERC-8004 registration, who cannot be clustered this way at all.
does_not_assert: Fraud, sybil intent, or wrongdoing. It is a shape in the data: many registrations from one address. Bulk minting is legal and often mundane.
That members of a cluster are controlled by one party today. Registrations are transferable.

pay.builder.attribution.v2.title: Counted payments carrying an app's Builder Code
pay.builder.attribution.v2.window: all time; transactions are read once
pay.builder.attribution.v2.definition: Counted payments whose transaction carries an ERC-8021 Builder Code: a suffix appended to the calldata by the app, wallet or agent framework that built the transaction. Reported as the USD attributed, the number of distinct codes, and the largest code's share of attributed USD.
pay.builder.attribution.v2.method: The transaction input is read from the public Base RPC and its ERC-8021 suffix parsed. Schema 0 carries comma-separated ASCII codes; schema 1 adds a custom registry; schema 2 is a CBOR map, shown as the app code followed by "w:<wallet code>" and "s:<service code>" (x402 payments settled by Coinbase's facilitator carry the wallet code cdp_facil1). A smart account (ERC-4337) carries the suffix at the end of its user operation's calldata, inside the bundle, and is read there. Codes are registered in the Base Builder Codes registry (0x000000BC7E6457e610fe52Dcc0ca5b3ce59C8E80).
excludes: Transactions not yet read (reported as pending in the note).
Suffixes whose schema the ERC does not define, which are counted as "schema:N" but not decoded.
does_not_assert: Who operates an app: a code names an app that attributed itself, and its registered metadata is usually private.
That payments without a code were not made through an app.
pay.builder.attribution.v2.note: Every counted payment read under v1 was read again with this parser on 13 October 2026; see /api/changepoints cp-2026-10-13-builder-parser for the counts before and after.

partner.virtuals.undergrad.v1.title: Virtuals identities still pre-graduation
partner.virtuals.undergrad.v1.definition: Identities in our ingested set whose status is UNDERGRAD — they have not graduated from the bonding curve.
partner.virtuals.undergrad.v1.method: Their own status field, counted on our rows.
excludes: Identities we have not ingested.
does_not_assert: Failure. Most of a launchpad catalog being pre-launch is what a launchpad looks like.
That these agents will never work. It says they have not started, which is why every rate over the whole catalog must be read against this number.

partner.x402.labeled_l7.v1.title: x402 payers with independent payment evidence
partner.x402.labeled_l7.v1.definition: Observed x402 payers that also have a verified payment made BEFORE their first x402 ticket, or to a counterparty that is not an x402 recipient.
partner.x402.labeled_l7.v1.method: The ticket being classified may not be the evidence that promotes its own payer. Without that rule every farm that pays once becomes a labelled live agent.
excludes: Evidence consisting only of the x402 tickets under classification.
does_not_assert: That unlabelled payers are farms. They are unlabelled, which means we have not joined them to an identity.

pay.excluded.preregistration.v1.title: Payment value excluded as pre-registration
pay.excluded.preregistration.v1.definition: Value moved by bound wallets BEFORE the registration they are bound to was minted, and therefore excluded from every published payment figure.
pay.excluded.preregistration.v1.method: Each registration's mint block is read from the Identity registry's ERC-721 mint. Any transfer earlier than that block is marked and stops counting.
does_not_assert: That these payments are illegitimate. They are simply not agent payments — they happened before the agent existed.

pay.topactor.share.v1.title: Share of observed value from the largest single actor
pay.topactor.share.v1.definition: The fraction of total observed payment value contributed by the single actor with the greatest observed value.
pay.topactor.share.v1.method: max(sum(amount_usd) grouped by actor) divided by the countable total.
excludes: The same exclusions as pay.usd.total.v1.
does_not_assert: That the largest actor is anomalous or wrong. It is published so the total can be read honestly, not to cast doubt on it.

pay.usd.by_day.v1.title: Counted agent spending by the day it was paid
pay.usd.by_day.v1.definition: The counted set of pay.usd.total.v1 (receipts checked, routing hops and money moved before registration left out) grouped by the UTC day of the payment's block time, as known at the time of publication. pay_usd_last_day is the last complete day; pay_usd_7d_avg and pay_usd_30d_avg are the means of the last 7 and 30 complete days. The full series is /api/payday.
pay.usd.by_day.v1.method: One SQL grouping of the payments table, hourly. The running total's day-to-day change is not used: it mixes payments made that day with older payments found that day.
excludes: The current UTC day and the one before it from the averages: they are still being found by the scan (provisional in /api/payday).
does_not_assert: That a day is final. A day's figure rises when the scan finds more of its payments, and falls if a receipt check later moves a payment out of the counted set.

pay.composition.v1.title: What counted spending consists of
pay.composition.v1.window: all time since each registration's mint block, as pay.usd.total.v1
pay.composition.v1.definition: The counted set of pay.usd.total.v1 (receipt read, routing hops and money moved before registration left out), taken apart in one pass, each payment in exactly one part, in this order: own_positions = into a lending or vault position the paying wallet still holds (receipt-proven, as pay.usd.ownpositions.v1); bridge, work_escrow and swap = to a destination our label map puts in that category; lending_other and yield_vault_other = to a labelled lending or vault contract where the receipt does not show the position credited back to the payer (or not yet checked); labelled_other = any other labelled category; agent_to_agent = to a wallet bound to another ERC-8004 registration; x402_sellers = to the payTo address of a seller listed in Coinbase's x402 Bazaar; unnamed = everything else. comp_total_usd is the total of the same pass, so the parts add up to it exactly.
pay.composition.v1.method: One grouping of the payments table by destination inside the counterparty-map run, every three hours; every part is written with the same timestamp. Metric keys: comp_total_usd and comp_<part>_usd.
excludes: Routing hops (pay.excluded.passthrough.v1).
Money moved before the registration existed (pay.excluded.preregistration.v1).
Payments whose receipt has not been read yet.
does_not_assert: That an unnamed payment is or is not commerce: unnamed means only that we have not labelled the destination.
That a bridge payment left its owner: pay.usd.leftcontrol.netbridge.v1 takes out the bridged money that arrived back at the paying wallet's own address.
That x402_sellers is all x402 spending. It counts payments sent straight to a Bazaar seller's payTo address; x402.observed.usd.v1 measures x402 settlements by its own method, so the two differ.

pay.excluded.passthrough.v1.title: Pass-through USD excluded from agent spending
pay.excluded.passthrough.v1.definition: USD value of outgoing USDC transfers from agent-bound wallets that were routing hops: money that arrived and left again on its way somewhere else, rather than the agent paying for something.
pay.excluded.passthrough.v1.method: Each observed payment is checked against the wallet's own inflows; a transfer that forwards funds it just received is marked pass_through and excluded from every spending total. The excluded amount is published so the exclusion can be audited, not just trusted.
excludes: Payments from before the agent was registered, which are excluded separately (pay.excluded.preregistration.v1).
does_not_assert: That pass-through money is illegitimate. Routing is a normal thing for a wallet to do; it is just not the agent spending.

pay.loops.v1.title: Circular payments in the counted set
pay.loops.v1.definition: Wallet pairs that paid each other in both directions within the counted set, the USD matched in both directions (the smaller of the two sums for each pair), and counted payments whose recipient is itself a wallet bound to an ERC-8004 identity.
pay.loops.v1.method: Self-join of counted payments on sender and recipient.
excludes: Loops that pass through wallets we do not watch.
does_not_assert: That reciprocal payments are wash trading: two agents can legitimately buy from each other.

pay.counterparties.v1.title: Distinct addresses agents have paid
pay.counterparties.v1.definition: Distinct recipient addresses across all observed agent payments.
pay.counterparties.v1.method: Counted from the same payment set, after the pre-registration exclusion.
excludes: Recipients of excluded payments.
does_not_assert: That each address is a distinct seller. Most are contracts, and one operator can run many.
That we know what any of them do. Where we can name one from a citable source we publish the label; most remain unnamed.

pay.events.v1.title: Observed agent payments
pay.events.v1.definition: USDC transfers we have watched leave a wallet bound to a tracked agent, dated after that agent's registration.
pay.events.v1.method: Asset-transfer scan per bound wallet. Every payment is dated against the mint date of its agent's registration, and anything earlier is held out of this count.
excludes: Transfers from before the agent existed. Counting those inflated our own headline by roughly three times before we read mint dates.
Inferred payments. If we did not observe the transfer, it is not here.
Assets other than USDC, and chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: That this is all agent payment activity. It is what we can see from wallets we have bound, which is a sample.
That each payment was autonomous. We observe a transfer, not the decision behind it.

platform.sdr.v1.title: Standardised Drain Ratio per launch platform
platform.sdr.v1.unit: ratio (1 = the market rate), with a 95% interval
platform.sdr.v1.window: the whole ranked cohort, from each agent's first left-control payment
platform.sdr.v1.definition: For each minting address with at least 30 ranked agents: drain-shaped incidents observed among its agents divided by the drains expected from the market-wide drain hazard (Nelson-Aalen over the whole cohort) given each agent's own time at risk. The standardised mortality ratio of clinical epidemiology, applied to agents. The 95% interval is Byar's approximation to the exact Poisson limits; a platform differs from the market only when its interval excludes 1.0.
platform.sdr.v1.method: afg-ladderdyn, daily, queries only. A minting address is a platform, a launchpad or a deployer, named by its label when it has one and by its address otherwise.
excludes: Minting addresses with fewer than 30 ranked agents.
Drains before the agent's first left-control payment.
does_not_assert: That a platform caused its agents' drains, or that it is a person: a minter is an address.
Precision: with few drains in the cohort, most intervals include 1.0, and that is the finding.

payers.set.v1.title: Payer set of an agent
payers.set.v1.definition: For one ERC-8004 agent on Base: the distinct addresses observed paying it, from (a) stablecoin transfers into its bound wallets read by the income scan (USDC, USDT, EURC, DAI) and (b) counted payments into its bound wallets from other registered agents' wallets read by the payment scan. Each with the number of payments, USD, first and last paid, which scan saw it, and the payer's own token id when the payer is a bound wallet.
payers.set.v1.method: money_events kind EARN for the agent plus kind PAY with to_id among the agent's open bindings; both exclude routing hops (money that left again in the same transaction), transfers before the payee was registered, and rows whose receipt is not read yet. Up to 250 payers listed, largest by USD first; payers_total is the full count. Published for use as clientAddresses in ERC-8004 getSummary, the reviewer filter the standard asks for because unfiltered feedback is Sybil-prone.
excludes: Payments before the agent's registration.
Routing hops.
Income older than the newest 50 stablecoin transfers at each read of a wallet (the income scan reads ranked wallets every 3 days from 27 Sep 2026).
Income into agents below L7, which the income scan does not read; their payer set holds only payments from other registered agents.
does_not_assert: That a payer is independent of the agent's operator.
That every payer is listed: observed payers are a lower bound.
payers.set.v1.source: AFG-Pulse income scan and payment scan

pay.usd.total.v1.title: Observed payment value
pay.usd.total.v1.window: all time since each registration's mint block
pay.usd.total.v1.definition: The summed USD value of every countable observed payment out of a bound wallet.
pay.usd.total.v1.method: Sum of amount_usd over money_events of kind PAY where pre_registration is false.
excludes: Pre-registration payments (see pay.excluded.preregistration.v1).
Payments from wallets whose registration has no mint date yet — held out until dated, never assumed.
does_not_assert: That this is the size of the agent economy. It is a sample: what we watched, from the wallets we have bound, on one chain, in one asset.
That the total is typical of its members — read pay.topactor.share.v1 and pay.usd.median.v1 beside it.

pay.usd.total.v2.title: Counted payment value
pay.usd.total.v2.window: all time since each registration's mint block
pay.usd.total.v2.definition: The summed USD value of every counted payment out of a wallet bound to a registered agent: a stablecoin transfer whose receipt was read, made after the registration existed, that was not a routing hop and did not go to one of the agent's own addresses.
pay.usd.total.v2.method: Sum of amount_usd over money_events of kind PAY with pre_registration false, pass_checked_at set and pass_through false. Since 21 Oct 2026 a transfer to one of the agent's own addresses (any wallet ever bound to it, its registration's current owner, the address it was minted to) is recorded in own_transfers and excluded the same way a routing hop is; the excluded amount is published as pay.excluded.ownaddress.v1. v1's text described only the pre-registration exclusion; the routing-hop and receipt-check rules had been applied since September without being written into it.
excludes: Pre-registration payments (pay.excluded.preregistration.v1).
Routing hops: money that arrived and left again on its way somewhere else (pay.excluded.passthrough.v1).
Transfers to the agent's own addresses: a payment is a change of who is entitled to the money, and moving it between one's own addresses is not one (pay.excluded.ownaddress.v1).
Payments whose receipt has not been read yet: held out until checked, never assumed.
does_not_assert: That this is the size of the agent economy. It is what we watched, from the wallets we have bound, on one chain, in stablecoins.
That the total is typical of its members: read pay.topactor.share.v1 and pay.usd.median.v1 beside it.
That the money was spent on goods or services: about half goes into positions the agent still holds (pay.composition.v1).

pay.excluded.ownaddress.v1.title: Transfers to an agent's own addresses, excluded from counted payments
pay.excluded.ownaddress.v1.definition: USD value of stablecoin transfers from a wallet bound to an agent to another of that agent's own addresses: any wallet ever bound to it, its registration's current owner, or the address it was minted to.
pay.excluded.ownaddress.v1.method: After the receipt check, each counted payment whose recipient is one of the agent's own addresses is recorded in own_transfers and excluded from every total. Published so the exclusion can be audited. First applied on 21 Oct 2026: 4,061 transfers, $688.05.
excludes: Transfers that never reached the counted set (pre-registration, routing hops, unchecked receipts).
does_not_assert: That the agent did anything wrong: moving money between one's own wallets is normal; it is just not paying someone.

pay.usd.ownpositions.v1.title: Counted payments into the payer's own positions
pay.usd.ownpositions.v1.window: all time since each registration's mint block
pay.usd.ownpositions.v1.definition: The part of the counted payment value that went into a lending market or vault position credited to the paying wallet itself: in the same transaction the payer is minted the position's claim token (vault shares, aTokens), or the market sends the payer its own token.
pay.usd.ownpositions.v1.method: For counted payments to recipients labelled lending or yield_vault (policy adapters included), the transaction receipt is read once and searched for an ERC-20 Transfer to the payer from the zero address, or from the recipient contract of its own token. Receipts from the public Base RPC.
excludes: Swaps: a token bought is an exchange, not a position in a market.
Bridges: money that leaves Base may still be the agent's, but a receipt on Base cannot show it.
Deposits whose receipt credits someone other than the payer.
does_not_assert: That the agent still holds the position today: withdrawals are separate inflows and can follow minutes later.
Anything about who operates the wallets, the adapter or the markets.

pay.usd.median.v1.title: Median observed payment
pay.usd.median.v1.definition: The median USD value of a single countable observed payment.
pay.usd.median.v1.method: percentile_cont(0.5) over amount_usd of countable PAY events.
excludes: The same exclusions as pay.usd.total.v1.
does_not_assert: That payments are distributed symmetrically. They are not: the mean is several times the median.

pay.usd.leftcontrol.v1.title: Counted payments less own positions
pay.usd.leftcontrol.v1.window: all time since each registration's mint block
pay.usd.leftcontrol.v1.definition: Counted payment value minus pay.usd.ownpositions.v1: what left the paying wallet's control on Base.

payee.facts.v1.title: Payee facts: seven measurable things about an address an agent is about to pay
payee.facts.v1.unit: per payee and per request: seven facts, each true, false or unavailable, with evidence and the time measured
payee.facts.v1.window: the payee's last 7 days of stablecoin transfers (302,400 blocks) for the transfer-based facts; the latest block for code; the agent's whole counted-payment history before the request for the history-based facts
payee.facts.v1.definition: For one receiving address on Base, the Gate reports: (1) relay_shape, whether at least 80% of the inbound stablecoin transfers in the window were forwarded (80% or more of the amount, same token) within 10 minutes, given at least 3 inbound transfers (gate/facts.mjs RELAY_SHARE = 0.8 for both); (2) swap_unfreezable, whether at least half of the window's stablecoin outflow went to addresses labelled as swap venues; (3) funded_by_exits_to, the top five funders and top five destinations by USD in the window, plus how many registered agents have paid the address; (4) poisoning_lookalike, whether the address shares its first 3 and last 4 hex characters with a different address the paying agent paid or was funded by; (5) sweeper_7702, whether the address is an EIP-7702 delegated account whose delegate code matches a known sweeper fingerprint (keccak-256 of the runtime code) or has the tiny forwarder shape (at most 256 bytes, with CALL and SELFBALANCE or CALLVALUE); (6) pay_on_proof_claim, whether a contract payee's runtime code carries a known claim selector (a 'pay on proof' claim that may not bind the payee); (7) fresh_destination_size, whether the paying agent never paid this address before and the requested amount exceeds its largest earlier counted payment.
payee.facts.v1.method: eth_getCode at latest for the payee and, if delegated, its delegate; eth_getLogs for Transfer events on the four verified stablecoin contracts with the payee as sender or recipient over the window, chunked; the counterparty preview (/api/counterparty) for registered payers; the agent's counted payments from the ledger for the history facts; the venue label map (gate/venues.json) for swap venues; research/sweepers.json for sweeper fingerprints. A fact whose channel fails is reported as unavailable with the reason, never as false.
excludes: Native ETH transfers (not stablecoin transfers).
Transfers older than the window.
Any judgement of the payee's business or identity.
Payees on chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: That a payee with a true fact is malicious, or that one with all facts false is legitimate.
That a claim selector means the claim is unsafe: whether it binds the payee needs the verified source.
That a look-alike was planted on purpose.
That the sweeper list is complete.
assumptions: The four stablecoin contracts and the venue labels are correct and current.
The agent's counted payments are complete for the history facts (the ledger's own set, not the 25-payment public view).
A log channel serves 7 days of Transfer events; without it the three transfer facts are unavailable.
known_gaps: On 14 Oct 2026 the free Base RPC endpoints served no (mainnet.base.org) or only the last ~4,000 blocks (publicnode) of logs, so the transfer facts could not be computed in the lab.
The sweeper fingerprint list holds 10 families, two verified on chain; a new delegate matches only through the tiny-forwarder shape.
Claim selectors are matched by PUSH4 scan of runtime code; proxies hide the implementation.
payee.facts.v1.intended_use: Facts an operator's policy reads before signing (block, warn or log per fact), and the evidence lines of a Gate decision.
payee.facts.v1.not_intended_for: A verdict on a payee; a score; a public list of bad addresses.
payee.facts.v1.cost_to_fake: A payee can avoid relay_shape by holding funds longer than 10 minutes, swap_unfreezable by exiting through an unlabelled venue, and fresh_destination_size by receiving a small first payment (which probe_then_large then scores); it cannot change its code kind or its funders' history after the fact, and a look-alike must still be a different address.
payee.facts.v1.threat_model: Assume the model behind an agent can be steered by text it reads (a prompt injection, a poisoned tool result, a planted memory): every signal here is measured from the chain and our ledger, never from what the agent says, and nothing here is a verdict on an agent, an operator or a person.
payee.facts.v1.source: afg-security-lab gate/ (facts.mjs, POLICY.md, SAMPLES.md), 2026-10-14; production: AFG-Pulse (afg-oochar, afg-intake gate routes), 16 Oct 2026
payee.facts.v1.status: live from 16 Oct 2026 (/api/gate/facts, payee_facts); facts describe an address, they do not judge it

pay.usd.leftcontrol.netbridge.v1.title: Left control, net of money bridged back to the same address
pay.usd.leftcontrol.netbridge.v1.chain_set: eip155:8453 (Base), with the destination chain of each followed bridge payment
pay.usd.leftcontrol.netbridge.v1.definition: Counted payments minus own positions (pay.usd.leftcontrol.v1, taken from the composition pass), minus the USD of bridged payments that arrived at the paying wallet's own address on the other chain (bridge.follow.back_to_payer.v1).
pay.usd.leftcontrol.netbridge.v1.method: comp_total_usd − comp_own_positions_usd − bridge_follow_back_to_payer_usd, written by the counterparty-map run. The back-to-payer figure is as of the bridge-follow run, which can be a few hours older.
excludes: Bridged money that went to a different address, or that we could not follow, stays in the figure.
does_not_assert: That the rest bought goods or services: it still includes swaps, escrow payments and unnamed destinations.

That a contract account's address on another chain belongs to the same party. For a plain key or an EIP-7702 account the same address means the same key; for a contract account it is probable, not proven.

poison.events.24h.v1.title: Poisoning transfers into agent wallets' history, last 24 hours
poison.events.24h.v1.definition: A poisoning transfer is (a) a Transfer of zero from the wallet in USDC, USDT, DAI, USDbC, EURC, WETH or cbBTC (anyone can call transferFrom for zero without an approval) to an address whose first 4 and last 4 hex characters both match a different payee of the wallet, or (b) a Transfer from the wallet in a token that is not one of those contracts but whose symbol, after removing accents and invisible characters and mapping look-alike letters (Cyrillic, Greek, Georgian, Lisu) to Latin, reads as one of them, sent to an address whose last 4 hex characters match one of the wallet's payees, or (c) any other token sent to an address that has no contract code and whose first 4 and last 4 hex characters both match a payee. Counted over the last 24 hours across every watched wallet.
poison.events.24h.v1.method: Every Base wallet that has made at least one counted agent payment (money_events kind PAY), with the payees it has paid. One eth_getLogs per 2,000 wallets returns every ERC-20 Transfer whose sender is one of them, from any token contract.
excludes: Fake-symbol tokens sent to addresses that resemble none of the wallet's payees (they are not tied to a payment to copy).
NFT transfers.
does_not_assert: That the wallet's owner noticed, or lost anything.
