probe.hosted_sink.v1.title: Share of descriptors on a shared host
probe.hosted_sink.v1.definition: Share of probed registrations whose URI points at a hosting service shared by many other registrations rather than at their own domain.
probe.hosted_sink.v1.method: Group resolved URIs by host and mark hosts carrying many distinct registrations.
excludes: Registrations with no resolvable URI.
does_not_assert: That shared hosting is illegitimate. It is cheap and sensible. It does mean a single host outage can take a large slice of the registry offline at once, and that concentration is worth seeing.

probe.domain.checked.v1.title: Registrations needing endpoint-domain verification
probe.domain.checked.v1.definition: In the probe sweep's uniform random sample, the registrations that declare at least one HTTPS service endpoint on a domain other than the one serving their registration file (or whose registration file is not served over HTTPS at all), so control of that endpoint domain is not shown by the registration itself.
probe.domain.checked.v1.method: ERC-8004, Endpoint Domain Verification (Optional): domain control is already shown when an endpoint sits on the domain that serves the registration file (same host, or one a subdomain of the other); every other HTTPS endpoint domain needs the well-known proof. Shared hosting platforms' submit URLs are excluded, as for L5.
does_not_assert: That an unverified endpoint is fake. The check is optional in the standard.

revisions.what: From the sweep at 22:16 UTC on 12 October 2026, two kinds of endpoint domain are not counted, because no agent can publish a proof there: profile links on shared public platforms (github.com, x.com, facebook.com, sites.google.com, farcaster.xyz, basescan.org and similar) and reserved example names (example.com, *.test). The first sweep, at 21:57 UTC on 12 October, counted them: 329 registrations, 1 verified.

probe.l1.uri_nonempty.v1.title: L1 — registration declares a URI
probe.l1.uri_nonempty.v1.definition: Share of probed registrations whose on-chain record contains a non-empty URI.
probe.l1.uri_nonempty.v1.method: Read the registration's stored URI and check it is not blank.
excludes: Registrations we could not read at all.
does_not_assert: That the URI resolves, or that anything is behind it. That is the next rung, and most of the fall-off happens there.

probe.l2.uri_2xx.v1.title: L2 — the URI answers
probe.l2.uri_2xx.v1.definition: Share of probed registrations whose declared URI returns a 2xx response.
probe.l2.uri_2xx.v1.method: One HTTP request per registration, with a timeout. A timeout is a failure, not a retry-until-success.
excludes: Registrations with no URI to fetch.
does_not_assert: That the response is an agent card, or valid, or truthful. A 200 from a parked domain counts here and fails the next rung.

probe.domain.tophost.v1.title: Endpoint-domain set: share on the most common host
probe.domain.tophost.v1.definition: Of the registrations counted by probe.domain.checked.v1, the share whose checked endpoint domains include the single most common one. A high share means the verified rate mostly describes one platform.
probe.domain.tophost.v1.method: Counted over the same sweep, from the endpoint domains read for probe.domain.verified.v1 (up to two per registration).
does_not_assert: Which platform it is; the host is in the probe log, not in this figure.

probe.hosted_sink.v2.title: Registrations listing a shared hosting sink
probe.hosted_sink.v2.definition: Share of the probe sample whose registration lists, among its first 8 web endpoints, a shared hosting platform's submit URL (agentverse.ai/v1/hosting/submit or /v1/submit).
probe.hosted_sink.v2.method: Read from the registration file, in any order; the sink itself is never requested.
does_not_assert: That the agent is fake. Hosted agents may be real; the sink just cannot show it.

probe.domain.verified.v1.title: Endpoint-domain verified rate
probe.domain.verified.v1.definition: Of the registrations counted by probe.domain.checked.v1, the share whose off-domain endpoint domains (up to two per registration) all serve https://{domain}/.well-known/agent-registration.json with a registrations entry whose agentRegistry (eip155:8453:0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432) and agentId match the on-chain agent.
probe.domain.verified.v1.method: One guarded GET per domain per sweep (8 s timeout, at most 3 redirects, 256 KB body cap, private addresses refused, nothing executed); the file must parse as JSON and carry a registrations list. The criterion is the one the standard gives readers for treating an endpoint domain as verified.
excludes: Endpoints that are not HTTPS (ENS names, DIDs, email, ipfs://).
Endpoints on the domain that serves the registration file.
does_not_assert: That the agent behind a verified domain works or is honest; only that whoever controls the domain says this registration is theirs.

revisions.what: Same scope change as probe.domain.checked.v1, from the 22:16 UTC sweep on 12 October 2026. On the first sweep 271 of the 329 registrations had their endpoint on one platform's API host, which published no proof file; probe.domain.tophost.v1 now reports that concentration with every sweep.

probe.domain.file.v1.title: Endpoint-domain proof file present
probe.domain.file.v1.definition: Of the registrations counted by probe.domain.checked.v1, the share for which at least one off-domain endpoint domain serves /.well-known/agent-registration.json at all (status 2xx), whether or not it lists this agent.
probe.domain.file.v1.method: Same fetch as probe.domain.verified.v1. The gap between this and the verified rate is domains that publish a file listing other agents, or a file without a registrations list.

probe.l3.schema_valid.v1.title: L3 — the document parses
probe.l3.schema_valid.v1.definition: Share of probed registrations whose URI returns a document that parses as the expected agent descriptor.
probe.l3.schema_valid.v1.method: Parse the response and check the required shape is present.
excludes: Registrations that never answered.
does_not_assert: That the contents are accurate. Schema validity means somebody filled in the right fields, not that the fields are true.

probe.l5.endpoint_live.v1.title: Live endpoint rate
probe.l5.endpoint_live.v1.definition: Share of a uniform random sample of registrations whose declared service endpoint returned a successful response to a plain GET.
probe.l5.endpoint_live.v1.method: Uniform random sample over the registry's token id space, then an HTTP probe with an 8 s timeout, at most 2 redirects, a 256 KB body cap, and no execution of anything returned.
excludes: Registrations whose only endpoint is a shared hosting platform's submit URL — that proves the platform is up and nothing about the agent. Those cap at L4.
does_not_assert: That the agent behind the endpoint works, only that something answered.

revisions.what: Superseded by probe.l5.endpoint_live.v2. This text said at most 2 redirects and that sink-only registrations cap at L4; the code followed 3 redirects, read only the first 4 listed entries, stopped at the first live one, and applied the sink cap only when the sink came before a live endpoint. v2 reads up to 8 web endpoints in any order, never probes a sink, and counts a completed protocol handshake as live.

probe.l5.endpoint_live.v2.title: Live endpoint rate
probe.l5.endpoint_live.v2.definition: Share of a uniform random sample of registrations with a readable registration file (L2), parseable fields (L3) and at least one declared entry (L4), of which at least one declared web endpoint, other than a shared hosting platform's submit URL, answers within 8 seconds: a 2xx or 402 to a GET, or a completed protocol handshake (probe.l6.protocol.v1).
probe.l5.endpoint_live.v2.method: Uniform random sample of 1,024 over the registry's token id space every six hours. Up to 8 web endpoints per registration (http, https or ipfs; ENS names, DIDs and emails are skipped), in any order. Every request goes through one sandbox: 8 s for the whole request, at most 3 redirects each re-checked, no private or reserved addresses, a 256 KB body cap, nothing returned is executed.
excludes: Shared hosting platforms' submit URLs (agentverse.ai/v1/hosting/submit and /v1/submit): they are never probed, because an answer proves the platform is up and nothing about the agent. A registration whose only web endpoints are those stays at L4.
does_not_assert: That the agent behind the endpoint works, only that something answered.

probe.l6.protocol.v1.title: Endpoints that speak an agent protocol
probe.l6.protocol.v1.definition: Share of the same sample whose registration reached L5 and at least one endpoint completed one of three handshakes: MCP (a POSTed initialize returns a JSON-RPC result with a protocolVersion string, as JSON or as one server-sent-event data line), A2A (an agent card, at the declared card URL or at /.well-known/agent-card.json or agent.json on the endpoint's host, that is a JSON object with a string name and a skills array), or x402 (a 402 whose body, or base64 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header, holds accepts[] with an entry naming a scheme, a network and a payTo address).
probe.l6.protocol.v1.method: The MCP handshake is sent only to endpoints the registration declares as MCP or whose path ends in /mcp or /sse; the A2A card is read only for endpoints declared as A2A or whose URL is a card; the x402 test reads the L5 response and sends nothing extra. Same sandbox as probe.l5.endpoint_live.v2. The first handshake that passes ends the check for that registration.
excludes: Protocols other than these three.
Endpoints on shared hosting platforms' submit URLs.
does_not_assert: That the tools, skills or paid resources do anything useful. A handshake shows the endpoint speaks the protocol, not that its service works or is safe.

rank.costtofake.v1.title: What the ranks cost to reach
rank.costtofake.v1.definition: Ranked identities (L7 and above) whose counted payments sum to less than one US dollar, and the smallest counted total among L9 identities.
rank.costtofake.v1.method: Sum of counted payments per ranked identity. Zero-value transfers, which anyone can emit from any address, are checked separately and are not in the counted set.
excludes: Payments outside the counted set.
does_not_assert: That a small total is fake: x402 micropayments are legitimately a fraction of a cent.
That the rank rules will change; this measures how cheap each rung is today.

probe.l4.services_declared.v1.title: L4 — the agent declares services
probe.l4.services_declared.v1.definition: Share of probed registrations whose descriptor declares at least one service or endpoint it offers.
probe.l4.services_declared.v1.method: Read the parsed descriptor and look for a non-empty service declaration.
excludes: Registrations whose document did not parse.
does_not_assert: That the service works, or is reachable, or has ever been paid for. Declaring a service is a claim by the operator; the ladder does not treat it as evidence of trade.

rank.independence.v1.title: Independence score (seed-based, best path)
rank.independence.v1.definition: 1 if, in the window, the agent made a counted payment that left its control (rank.l7plus.v2) to a seed; otherwise 0.5 times the best score of any agent OUTSIDE the agent's own operator set that paid one of the agent's payees, over at most three hops: the single best path from a seed, with the product of decays along it, never a sum. A seed is an address paid in such payments by agents from at least three different operator sets, or an address carrying a label (an exchange, a bridge, a venue, a protocol); bot-like contracts (counterparty.botlike.v1) are not seeds. An operator set (cluster.ratio.v1) is the registrations tied by the same bound wallet, the same current owner, the same minter or the same first funder, each link ignored when it ties more than 50 registrations.
rank.independence.v1.method: afg-independence, daily at 03:10 UTC, from money_events, bindings, registry owners, mints and first funders. Cheng & Friedman (2005) prove that no symmetric score (one that depends only on graph shape, such as a count of counterparties) is sybilproof, and that a seed-based score with diminishing returns aggregated by the best path is; this is that score. Fresh identities in the agent's own set never help it; identities outside it help only by paying seeds themselves.
excludes: Payments into the agent's own positions, to its own addresses, or bridged back to it (rank.l7plus.v2).
Routing hops (pass-through) and payments before registration.
does_not_assert: That a score of 1 means a good agent: it means the agent paid something with demand from three or more operators.
That two registrations in one operator set belong to one person: they share a chain fact.
That the seed set is complete: a service paid by two operators only is not yet a seed.

probe.sample.size.v1.title: Registrations probed
probe.sample.size.v1.definition: How many registrations the endpoint sweep actually tested.
probe.sample.size.v1.method: An even sample across the registry rather than the newest or the busiest, so the ladder rates below describe the registry rather than its most active corner.
excludes: Registrations outside the sample.
does_not_assert: That the sample is large enough for any particular subgroup. It supports registry-wide rates, not per-operator claims.

rank.l8plus.v2.title: Actor at liveness 8 or above
rank.l8plus.v2.definition: Everything rank.l7plus.v1 requires, and the agent's bound wallet still holds at least $10 in stablecoins (USDC, USDT, EURC at the day's EUR/USD rate, and DAI) at our most recent balance read. An agent with more than one bound wallet counts its largest float.
rank.l8plus.v2.method: balanceOf for the four stablecoins via Multicall3 over every ranked wallet, every six hours, and again at the moment an evidence pack is bought. The rank is recomputed from those reads by one set-based statement after each payment scan.
excludes: Wallets whose balance we have not read.
Other tokens: ETH, wrapped ETH, LP and vault shares do not count toward the $10.
does_not_assert: That the balance is the agent's operating budget, or that anyone intends to spend it.
That an L8 agent is independent. Operators of fleets top many wallets up to just over $10 and spend them down, so the L8 count moves in steps when they do; rank.l9.v2 is the steadier measure.
rank.l8plus.v2.note: Published 12 October 2026. From 27 September 2026 the L8 line read the four-stablecoin float while rank.l8plus.v1 still said USDC; this version states the rule the counts have followed since then. The counts did not change on 12 October.

revisions.what: Superseded by rank.l8plus.v3, which rests on rank.l7plus.v2. 562 agents were L8+ under this definition at 12:53 UTC on 13 October 2026, 557 under v3; see /api/changepoints cp-2026-10-13-ladder-v2.

rank.l9.independent.v1.title: L9 agents with three independent counterparties
rank.l9.independent.v1.window: counterparties paid in the last 30 days
rank.l9.independent.v1.definition: Of the agents at L9 (rank.l9.v2: three or more counterparties in 30 days), those with at least three counterparties that are independent of the agent: an address with contract code (a venue, protocol or escrow), or an address that at least two different registered agents pay in counted payments. An address only this agent pays may be its operator's own, so it does not count here.
rank.l9.independent.v1.method: Counted payments (receipt read, no routing hops, nothing before registration) from money_events; contract code from the counterparty table (eth_getCode); the number of distinct paying agents per address over all counted payments. Published beside actors_l9, not instead of it, by the payment scan.
excludes: Agents below L9.
does_not_assert: That an excluded counterparty belongs to the agent's operator: only that nothing in our data shows anyone else pays it.
That a contract counterparty is independent of the operator: a fleet can pay its own contract.

revisions.what: Folded into the rank itself: rank.l9.v3 requires three independent counterparties, so from 13 October 2026 actors_l9_independent carries the L9 count under rank.l9.v3.

rank.l8plus.v3.title: Actor at liveness 8 or above
rank.l8plus.v3.definition: Everything rank.l7plus.v2 requires, and a bound wallet holds at least $10 in stablecoins (USDC, USDT, EURC at the day's EUR/USD rate, and DAI) at our most recent balance read. An agent with more than one bound wallet counts its largest float.
rank.l8plus.v3.method: As rank.l8plus.v2: balanceOf for the four stablecoins via Multicall3 over every ranked wallet, every six hours, and again when an evidence pack is bought.
excludes: Wallets whose balance we have not read.
Other tokens: ETH, wrapped ETH, LP and vault shares do not count toward the $10.
does_not_assert: That the balance is the agent's operating budget, or that anyone intends to spend it.
That an L8 agent is independent. Fleets top many wallets up to just over $10; rank.l9.v3 is the steadier measure.

rank.l8plus.v1.title: Actor at liveness 8 or above
rank.l8plus.v1.definition: Everything rank.l7plus.v1 requires, and the paying wallet still holds at least $10 of USDC at our most recent balance read.
rank.l8plus.v1.method: USDC balanceOf via Multicall3 over every ranked wallet, every six hours, and again at the moment an evidence pack is bought.
excludes: Wallets whose balance we have not read.
Non-USDC holdings. USDT, EURC and DAI balances are read alongside and published on the record as stables_float and float_breakdown, but the L8 line is still USDC until this definition is versioned.
does_not_assert: That the balance is the agent's operating budget, or that anyone intends to spend it.

revisions.what: Superseded by rank.l8plus.v2. From 27 September 2026 the L8 line read the four-stablecoin float while this text still said USDC.

rank.inflation.v1.title: Inflation ratio of an agent's L9 support
rank.inflation.v1.unit: ratio (1 = none of its L9 support comes from its own operator set)
rank.inflation.v1.definition: The agent's count of independent counterparties under rank.l9.v3 (contract code, or paid by two or more agents) divided by the same count when the second payer must come from a different operator set (cluster.ratio.v1) and bot-like contracts (counterparty.botlike.v1) do not count. null when the second count is zero while the first is not: all of its L9 support comes from its own set. The MeritRank attacker's gain (Nasrulin et al. 2022: reputation with the sybil edges over reputation without), read on L9's own rule.
rank.inflation.v1.method: afg-independence, daily. The agents whose cluster-aware count falls below three while rank.l9.v3 holds are the measured size of the gap the ladder page states (two agents of one operator paying the same addresses); published as l9_lose_cluster_aware.
excludes: Agents with no left-control payment in the window.
does_not_assert: That an inflated agent is a fleet: a builder testing two of its own agents against one escrow leaves the same shape.

rank.l9.v1.title: Actor at liveness 9
rank.l9.v1.window: rolling 30 days for the counterparty count
rank.l9.v1.definition: Everything rank.l8plus.v1 requires, and payments to three or more DISTINCT counterparty addresses within the last 30 days.
rank.l9.v1.method: Distinct to-addresses over the window, counted from observed transfers.
excludes: Repeat payments to the same address, which count once however often they recur.
does_not_assert: That the counterparties are unrelated to each other or to the agent.

revisions.what: Superseded by rank.l9.v2, with rank.l8plus.v2.

rank.l7plus.v1.title: Actor at liveness 7 or above
rank.l7plus.v1.window: all time since the registration's mint block
rank.l7plus.v1.definition: An ERC-8004 registration for which we have observed at least one non-inferred outbound stablecoin payment, from a wallet bound to that registration, to a DIFFERENT address.
rank.l7plus.v1.method: alchemy_getAssetTransfers over the stablecoins on Base (USDC; and since 27 September 2026 USDT, EURC and DAI, with EURC converted at the day's EURC/USD), filtered to transfers out of a bound wallet, plus Alchemy address-activity pushes for ranked wallets. The binding comes from ownerOf() on the Identity registry, or from an agentWallet declared in the registration file. Each payment carries its asset on the record.
excludes: Self-transfers — moving your own money between your own wallets is not paying a counterparty.
Any payment whose block time precedes the registration's mint block. A wallet may have been a person's for years before it was bound to an agent.
Payments by an actor whose registration has since changed hands, from the moment the binding closes.
does_not_assert: That the agent is autonomous. We cannot see whether a human approved the payment.
That the wallet is controlled by the registrant, only that it is bound by one of the recorded methods.
Anything about what the payment was for.

revisions.what: The method was extended from USDC to USDT, EURC and DAI, written into the method text. Counts rose as more history became visible; see the changepoint cp-2026-09-27-sweep at /api/changepoints.

Superseded by rank.l7plus.v2 (ladder v2): L7 now needs a payment that left the agent's control, not one into its own position, to its own address, or bridged back to itself. On the switch at 12:54 UTC, 7,866 agents were L7+ under this definition and 7,525 under v2; see /api/changepoints cp-2026-10-13-ladder-v2.

rank.l7plus.v2.title: Actor at liveness 7 or above (money left its control)
rank.l7plus.v2.window: all time since the registration's mint block
rank.l7plus.v2.definition: An ERC-8004 registration with at least one counted, non-inferred stablecoin payment from a wallet bound to it that LEFT the agent's control: the receiver is not a lending or vault position the transaction receipt shows the agent still holds, not one of the agent's own addresses (any wallet ever bound to it, the registration's current owner, the address it was minted to), and the payment is not a bridge leg that arrived back at the payer (the same address on the other chain, or followed to the payer).
rank.l7plus.v2.method: Payments: alchemy_getAssetTransfers over USDC, USDT, EURC and DAI on Base out of every bound wallet, every three hours; 519 wallets ranked before the 27 September 2026 census are also pushed in real time by an address-activity webhook. Counted means the receipt was read, the transfer is not a routing hop inside a larger transaction, and it happened after the registration was minted. Own positions: receipts show a claim token minted or a market token returned to the payer in the same transaction (pay.usd.ownpositions.v1). Bridges: legs followed by the bridge-status worker (pay.usd.leftcontrol.netbridge.v1). Recomputed for every actor after each payment scan, every three hours, by one set-based statement; the publish gate runs the same SQL.
excludes: Payments into the agent's own lending or vault position, proven from the receipt.
Payments to the agent's own addresses: wallets bound to it at any time, its registration's owner, its minter.
Bridge legs that arrived back at the paying wallet.
Everything rank.l7plus.v1 excluded: payments before the mint block, routing hops, inferred payments.
does_not_assert: That the agent is autonomous. We cannot see whether a human approved the payment.

That the receiver is unrelated to the operator. An operator can pay a fresh address of its own that nothing links to the agent; rank.l9.v3 adds the independence test, and rank.costtofake.v1 publishes what the ranks cost to reach.
Anything about what the payment was for.
rank.l7plus.v2.source: AFG-Pulse payment scan, investigations and bridge follow

rank.l9.v2.title: Actor at liveness 9
rank.l9.v2.window: rolling 30 days for the counterparty count
rank.l9.v2.definition: Everything rank.l8plus.v2 requires, and counted payments to three or more DISTINCT counterparty addresses within the last 30 days.
rank.l9.v2.method: Distinct to-addresses over the window, counted from the payments rank.l7plus.v1 counts (receipt read, no routing hops, nothing before registration, nothing inferred).
excludes: Repeat payments to the same address, which count once however often they recur.
does_not_assert: That the counterparties are unrelated to each other or to the agent: three addresses funded by the same operator qualify. rank.costtofake.v1 publishes what the rank costs to reach.
rank.l9.v2.note: Published 12 October 2026 with rank.l8plus.v2, which it rests on. The counts did not change on 12 October.

revisions.what: Superseded by rank.l9.v3: the three counterparties must be independent (contract code, or paid by two or more agents) and paid with money that left the agent's control. 118 agents were L9 under this definition at 12:53 UTC on 13 October 2026, 74 under v3; see /api/changepoints cp-2026-10-13-ladder-v2.

rank.l9.v4.title: Actor at liveness 9 (independent counterparties, operator-set aware)
rank.l9.v4.window: rolling 30 days for the counterparty count
rank.l9.v4.definition: Everything rank.l8plus.v3 requires, and its payments that left its control (rank.l7plus.v2) reached at least three INDEPENDENT counterparties within the last 30 days. A counterparty is independent when it is a contract that is not bot-like (counterparty.botlike.v1), or when at least one registered agent OUTSIDE the paying agent's operator set (cluster.ratio.v1: same bound wallet, same current owner, same minter or same first funder, each link ignored above 50 registrations) also pays it in counted payments.
rank.l9.v4.method: Distinct receiving addresses over the window among the payments rank.l7plus.v2 counts; contract code from the counterparty table; bot-like contracts from the daily receipt check; the operator sets from agent_clusters, rebuilt daily. Measured before the switch on 13 October 2026 (20:19 UTC): 71 of the 72 L9 agents kept the level under this rule; applied 13 October 2026 at 21:22 UTC with 72 agents at L9 under both rules at that instant.
excludes: Repeat payments to the same address, which count once however often they recur.
An address only this agent and its own operator set pay.
A contract that forwards what it receives in the same transaction, is unverified, unlabelled and paid from at most two operator sets (bot-like).
does_not_assert: That two registrations in one operator set belong to one person: they share a chain fact.
That the operator sets are complete: an operator that funds each agent from a fresh address leaves no link, so this rule closes the simplest case only.

rank.l9.v3.title: Actor at liveness 9 (independent counterparties)
rank.l9.v3.window: rolling 30 days for the counterparty count
rank.l9.v3.definition: Everything rank.l8plus.v3 requires, and its payments that left its control (rank.l7plus.v2) reached at least three INDEPENDENT counterparties within the last 30 days. A counterparty is independent when it has contract code (a venue, protocol or escrow) or when at least two different registered agents pay it in counted payments.
rank.l9.v3.method: Distinct receiving addresses over the window among the payments rank.l7plus.v2 counts; contract code from the counterparty table (eth_getCode); the number of distinct paying agents per address over all counted payments. This is the test published beside L9 as rank.l9.independent.v1 from 12 October 2026, now the rule itself.
excludes: Repeat payments to the same address, which count once however often they recur.
An address only this agent pays: it may be the operator's own.
does_not_assert: That an excluded counterparty belongs to the operator: only that nothing in our data shows anyone else pays it.
That a contract counterparty is independent of the operator: a fleet can pay its own contract.

revisions.what: Superseded by rank.l9.v4: the second payer of a shared address must come from a different operator set, and bot-like contracts do not count. Measured before the switch: 71 of 72 L9 agents kept the level; at the switch (13 Oct, 21:22 UTC) 72 under both rules.

rank.survival.km.v1.title: Time from registration to first counted payment
rank.survival.km.v1.window: from each identity's mint to the time of measurement
rank.survival.km.v1.definition: The probability that an ERC-8004 identity on Base has made its first counted payment within t days of its mint, estimated with the Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator; identities that have not paid are censored at the time of measurement.
rank.survival.km.v1.method: Mint time from the registry (or the dated census); first payment is the earliest counted payment. Cohorts by the minting address's total mints on Base: single (1), 2-9, 10-99, 100-999, 1000 and more. Published at 365 days, with the median days to a first payment among identities that paid.
excludes: Identities without a mint time.
Payments excluded from the counted set (pre-registration, routing hops).
does_not_assert: That an identity that has not paid is idle: it may pay from a wallet we have not bound.
Why burst-minted identities pay less often; only that they do.

reg.burstminted.rate.v1.title: Share of the registry that arrived in bursts
reg.burstminted.rate.v1.definition: Burst-minted registrations divided by all registrations minted.
reg.burstminted.rate.v1.method: Arithmetic on the two counts above.
excludes: The same undercount at hour boundaries.
does_not_assert: That the remainder was organic. It is a floor on scripted minting, not a measure of authenticity.

reg.burstminted.v1.title: Registrations minted in bursts
reg.burstminted.v1.definition: Registrations minted as part of a run of 25 or more from a single address inside one hour.
reg.burstminted.v1.method: Group mints by address and hour; count those in hours meeting the threshold. The threshold is a stated choice, not a natural boundary — it is published so a reader can disagree with it.
excludes: Bursts spread across an hour boundary, which this undercounts.
does_not_assert: That burst-minted registrations are worthless. They are the signature of a script rather than of people signing up one at a time, and that distinction matters when the registry count is quoted as adoption.

reg.minted.base.v1.title: Registrations minted on Base
reg.minted.base.v1.definition: Every ERC-8004 Identity registration ever minted on Base, counted from the registry's own ERC-721 mint transfers, each with the exact block it landed in.
reg.minted.base.v1.method: alchemy_getAssetTransfers over the Identity contract, category erc721, transfers from the zero address.
excludes: Other chains. Public counters that report a much larger number are summing several chains.
does_not_assert: That this is a count of agents. It is a count of names issued — see reg.transferred.v1 and reg.burstminted.rate.v1 for why those differ.

reg.bursthours.v1.title: Hours containing a minting burst
reg.bursthours.v1.definition: How many distinct address-hours met the burst threshold.
does_not_assert: That each burst is a separate operator or a separate incident.

reg.minted.daily.v1.title: Registrations minted per day
reg.minted.daily.v1.definition: The number of ERC-8004 registrations minted on Base during a complete UTC day, counted from the registry's own ERC-721 mint transfers.
reg.minted.daily.v1.method: Grouped from the mint block timestamp of every registration we have dated. The current day is never published: a day's count is not a fact until the day is over.
excludes: The running current day.
Other chains.
does_not_assert: That the registrations represent distinct operators — see the minting-concentration finding, where one address accounts for an eighth of the registry.
reg.minted.daily.v1.supersedes_in_practice: A cited daily feed we previously relied on, which froze at the same value for two consecutive days while the chain kept moving.

reg.top10minter.share.v1.title: Share of the registry minted by ten addresses
reg.top10minter.share.v1.definition: Registrations minted by the ten busiest addresses, divided by all registrations minted.
reg.top10minter.share.v1.method: As above, taking the top ten.
does_not_assert: That the ten are unrelated to each other.

reg.minters.v1.title: Distinct addresses that minted registrations
reg.minters.v1.definition: How many distinct addresses have minted at least one registration.
reg.minters.v1.method: Group mints by recipient address. The address set behind this is published in full.
excludes: Chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: That each address is a distinct person or company. One operator can mint from many addresses, which would make the concentration below an understatement rather than an overstatement.

reg.transferred.rate.v1.title: Share of registrations that have changed hands
reg.transferred.rate.v1.definition: Registrations that have been transferred at least once, divided by all registrations minted.
reg.transferred.rate.v1.method: Distinct transferred token ids over the mint count.
excludes: Transfers we have not swept yet.
does_not_assert: That an identity was sold to a new operator. A transferable identity means a reputation history can change owner without any signal to the people relying on it — that is the reason to publish this, not a claim that it has happened commercially.

reg.topminter.share.v1.title: Share of the registry minted by one address
reg.topminter.share.v1.definition: Registrations minted by the single busiest address, divided by all registrations minted.
reg.topminter.share.v1.method: Group mints by address, take the largest, divide by the total.
does_not_assert: That those registrations are fake. Bulk minting is legitimate for a platform issuing identities on behalf of users. It does mean the headline registry count is not a count of independent participants, and reading it as one is the mistake this number exists to prevent.

rep.agents.rated.v1.title: Registrations that have received feedback
rep.agents.rated.v1.definition: Distinct registrations with at least one on-chain feedback event against them.
rep.agents.rated.v1.method: Read from the ERC-8004 Reputation registry's own logs on the keyless Base mesh.
excludes: Feedback on chains we do not scan.
does_not_assert: That a rated agent is a real or active one. Ten addresses wrote half of all feedback, much of it covering agents they cannot plausibly have transacted with.

reg.transferred.v1.title: Registrations that changed hands
reg.transferred.v1.definition: Registrations transferred at least once after minting — a secondary transfer, not a mint.
reg.transferred.v1.method: Same sweep as reg.minted.base.v1; transfers whose from-address is not the zero address.
excludes: Mints.
does_not_assert: That the agent changed. Only that the holder did.

reg.transfers.v1.title: Registration transfer events
reg.transfers.v1.definition: Secondary transfers of registration tokens — moves after the original mint.
reg.transfers.v1.method: Read from the Identity registry's own transfer log, excluding mints.
excludes: Mints, which are counted separately.
does_not_assert: That a transfer is a sale. It could be a custody move between wallets of the same operator, and nothing on-chain distinguishes the two.

rep.feedback.24h.v1.title: Feedback events in the last 24 hours
rep.feedback.24h.v1.definition: Feedback events recorded in the last day.
rep.feedback.24h.v1.method: Counted from our own ingest. Withheld entirely while the scan is behind the chain head — mid-backfill this measures how far we have read rather than what happened, and publishing that zero would be a false statement about the world.
excludes: Events in blocks we have not reached.
does_not_assert: That the day's activity is organic.

rep.raters.v1.title: Distinct addresses that have left feedback
rep.raters.v1.definition: Distinct client addresses appearing as the author of a feedback event.
rep.raters.v1.method: Group feedback events by their indexed author address.
excludes: Chains we do not scan.
does_not_assert: That the raters are independent. A large rater count sits alongside extreme concentration by volume, and the concentration is the more informative half.

rep.grounded.base.v1.title: Reviewer-agent pairs checked for payment
rep.grounded.base.v1.definition: Distinct (reviewer address, agent) pairs in ERC-8004 feedback on Base where the agent is one whose income we read (ranked agents, read by the income scan). The base of rep.grounded.share.v1.
rep.grounded.base.v1.method: reputation_feedback (chain 8453) grouped by lower-cased client address and agent, kept when the agent has any income row from the income scan.
excludes: Feedback on agents whose income we do not read: there, no payer seen means not looked.
rep.grounded.base.v1.source: AFG-Pulse reputation ingest and income scan

rep.grounded.v1.title: Payment-grounded feedback
rep.grounded.v1.definition: Of one agent's ERC-8004 feedback entries on Base, those whose client address is in the agent's payer set (payers.set.v1) with a first payment earlier than the feedback. Reported as a count and as a share of the agent's feedback entries.
rep.grounded.v1.method: Feedback from the Reputation Registry (afg-reputation, NewFeedback events, chain 8453) joined to payers.set.v1 on the client address; the payment must precede the feedback block time.
excludes: Feedback on other chains.
Payments the scans did not observe (see payers.set.v1).
does_not_assert: That grounded feedback is honest or independent: one operator can pay its own agent and rate it. On 12 Oct 2026 one agent's 85 feedback entries all came from a single wallet that had paid it 45 times.
That ungrounded feedback is fake: the reviewer may have paid through a route the scans do not read.
rep.grounded.v1.source: AFG-Pulse reputation ingest, income scan and payment scan

rep.feedback.total.v1.title: On-chain agent feedback events
rep.feedback.total.v1.window: all time since the registry's first event
rep.feedback.total.v1.definition: Feedback events emitted by the ERC-8004 Reputation registry, read from the registry's own logs.
rep.feedback.total.v1.method: Log scan over the keyless public Base mesh, which serves 10,000-block ranges where the paid tier caps at ten. No ABI was published, so the event layout was recovered from real logs: the rated agent id and the rater address are indexed topics, followed by two tag strings and two URIs.
excludes: Events on other chains.
Any field whose meaning the bytes do not make unambiguous.
does_not_assert: That feedback is true, earned, or disinterested. It is somebody's opinion published on-chain, and it can be bought as easily as it can be earned.
That the numeric fields are scores. One ranges from 5 to 1e20 across observed events — the shape of a token amount, not a rating — so it is published unnamed rather than guessed at.
That a rated agent is a working agent. Rating and observed payment are independent facts; the overlap between them is published separately.
rep.feedback.total.v1.note: Reputation is a SIGNAL and carries no weight in the L0-L9 ladder. Ten addresses wrote roughly four fifths of all feedback on this registry, so a rank that counted vouches would be climbable by ten addresses.

rep.grounded.share.v1.title: Payment-grounded feedback share (reviewer-agent pairs)
rep.grounded.share.v1.definition: Of the pairs in rep.grounded.base.v1, the share where the reviewer paid the agent, in a counted transfer, before its first rating: the share of feedback a payer filter (ERC-8004 getSummary with the payer set as clientAddresses) would keep.
rep.grounded.share.v1.method: A payment is an income-scan transfer into the agent's bound wallets, or a counted payment from another registered agent's wallet to them; routing hops, transfers before registration and unread receipts are excluded, as in payers.set.v1. Counted per pair, not per entry: on 12 Oct 2026 one wallet's 85 ratings of one agent it pays were 85 of the 102 grounded entries, 1 of the 6 grounded pairs.
excludes: Payments the scans did not observe (payers.set.v1 is a lower bound).
does_not_assert: That a grounded review is independent or honest.
That an ungrounded review is fake.
rep.grounded.share.v1.source: AFG-Pulse reputation ingest, income scan and payment scan

rep.rated.l7.v1.title: Rated agents we have also watched pay
rep.rated.l7.v1.definition: Agents that both received on-chain feedback and were independently observed making a real payment.
rep.rated.l7.v1.method: The intersection of the reputation set and the L7 set. This is the overlap between what somebody says about an agent and what we watched it do.
excludes: Agents outside our tracked set.
does_not_assert: That the feedback about them is accurate. The overlap is small, which is itself the point: reputation and observed behaviour are currently almost disjoint populations.

rep.top10rater.share.v1.title: Share of feedback written by the ten busiest raters
rep.top10rater.share.v1.definition: Feedback events authored by the ten most prolific rater addresses, divided by all feedback events.
rep.top10rater.share.v1.method: Group every event by its indexed rater address, take the ten largest, divide by the total.
does_not_assert: That prolific rating is dishonest. Bulk rating is a legitimate thing for an indexer or a scoring service to do — it just means the signal describes those services rather than a crowd.
That the ten addresses are distinct parties. One operator running ten raters would look identical from outside.

sol.agents.pay.30d.v1.title: What Solana agents and their owners paid, last 30 days
sol.agents.pay.30d.v1.definition: USDC and USDT that left the agent's own wallet (the MPL Core asset-signer address) and the owner wallets of Metaplex MPL Agent Registry agents, after the owner's first registration. The amount is the address's net USDC or USDT change in the transaction, so money that arrives and leaves in one transaction nets to zero. Published: owners paying and their outflow, agent wallets paying and their outflow, and payments whose largest recipient is an x402 Bazaar seller on Solana.
sol.agents.pay.30d.v1.method: Registration time from the oldest signature on each identity record (the asset's when the record has none); token accounts from getTokenAccountsByOwner (classic Token program, refreshed daily); signatures per token account from a cursor; each transaction read once with getTransaction (jsonParsed). Public Solana nodes first, Alchemy capped per run. Published only when every account is backfilled and the queue is empty.
excludes: Swaps: a transaction where the address also received another token or SOL, or that ran Jupiter, Raydium, Orca, Meteora, pump.fun, Phoenix or SolFi.
Transfers before the owner's first registration.
Token-2022 balances and SOL payments.
does_not_assert: That an owner's payment is agent spending: an owner wallet belongs to a person or a company.
Never added to any Base figure.

rep.toptag.share.v1.title: Share of feedback carrying the single most common tag
rep.toptag.share.v1.definition: Feedback events carrying the most frequent tag, divided by all feedback events.
rep.toptag.share.v1.method: Group by tag and take the largest. Grouping by author shows ten addresses wrote half the ratings; grouping by tag shows one vouching programme wrote nearly three quarters of them.
excludes: Events with no readable tag.
does_not_assert: That the tag is meaningless. It asserts that on-chain reputation is currently dominated by one programme, so treating the total as a broad social signal would misread it.

rep.toprater.share.v1.title: Share of feedback written by the single busiest rater
rep.toprater.share.v1.definition: Feedback events authored by the most prolific address, divided by all feedback events.
rep.toprater.share.v1.method: Group by author address and take the largest.
does_not_assert: That prolific rating is dishonest. Bulk rating is a legitimate thing for an indexer to do — it just means the signal describes that indexer rather than a crowd.

sol.agents.uri.v1.title: Solana registrations that point to a registration file
sol.agents.uri.v1.definition: Records of sol.agents.registered.v1 whose asset still exists and carries an AgentIdentity plugin with a URI.
sol.agents.uri.v1.method: Alchemy DAS getAssets, external_plugins of type AgentIdentity.
excludes: Assets that no longer exist.
does_not_assert: That the URI answers.

sol.agents.cards.v1.title: Solana agent cards: retrievable, valid, declaring a service
sol.agents.cards.v1.window: registration files probed so far (up to 400 a run, oldest checked first)
sol.agents.cards.v1.definition: Of registration files fetched through our probe sandbox: the share that answered (L2), the share that parse as an agent registration (L3), and the share that declare at least one service endpoint (L4), graded exactly as Base cards. Also published: the number of files probed and how many declare x402 support.
sol.agents.cards.v1.method: lib/probe.mjs: SSRF-guarded fetch, 8 s timeout, 256 KB cap, then the same grading as the Base liveness ladder.
excludes: Files not yet probed.
does_not_assert: That a declared service works or takes payment.

sol.agents.registered.v1.title: Agents registered on Solana (Metaplex registry)
sol.agents.registered.v1.definition: Every record of the Metaplex MPL Agent Registry on Solana: one Agent Identity record (program 1DREGFgysWYxLnRnKQnwrxnJQeSMk2HmGaC6whw2B2p) per registered agent, pointing at an MPL Core asset whose AgentIdentity plugin holds the registration URI, read with getProgramAccounts on public Solana nodes. Also published: distinct asset owners and the largest owner's share of registrations.
sol.agents.registered.v1.method: getProgramAccounts on the Agent Identity program; owners from Alchemy's DAS getAssets.
excludes: Agents registered anywhere else on Solana.
does_not_assert: That a registration is a working agent: it is issuance, like an ERC-8004 mint.

sol.agents.wallets.v1.title: Solana agent wallets holding USDC
sol.agents.wallets.v1.definition: For each existing asset, its MPL Core asset-signer address (derived from the asset; in 60 of the first 74 registration files that state a wallet address it is this one): USDC balance and SOL balance. Published: wallets read, wallets holding at least 1 USDC, and their USDC total.
excludes: Wallets other than the asset signer, such as an operator's own wallet.
does_not_assert: That a funded wallet has paid anyone.

stability.heartbeat.v1.title: Heartbeat: scheduled, irregular or bursty
stability.heartbeat.v1.unit: class, with the dispersion index and the gap CV
stability.heartbeat.v1.definition: For each agent at L7 or above with at least 10 counted payments in the window: the dispersion index I = variance / mean of its daily payment counts, and the coefficient of variation of the gaps between its payments. scheduled = I at most 0.8 and gap CV at most 0.6 (a clock-driven caller); bursty = I at least 3 or gap CV at least 1.5 (retries, batches); irregular otherwise; sparse = fewer than 10 payments in the window.
stability.heartbeat.v1.method: afg-stability, daily, queries only. The dispersion index is the point-process diagnostic in Cui (2022): I near 1 is Poisson, below 1 regular, above 1 self-exciting.
excludes: Agents with fewer than 10 counted payments in the window (sparse).
does_not_assert: That a bursty agent is retrying or failing: a batch job leaves the same shape.
Anything about payment value: the classes are read on timing alone.

stable.float.v1.title: Total stablecoin float
stable.float.v1.definition: The aggregate circulating supply of stablecoins across all chains, as reported by DefiLlama.
stable.float.v1.method: Read from DefiLlama's stablecoins endpoint. We do not reproduce it.
excludes: Anything DefiLlama does not track.
does_not_assert: That this money is available to agents, or connected to them in any way. It is the pool the agent economy is drawn from, published as context so a reader can see how small the measured agent numbers are beside it.
That the figure is precise. Stablecoin supply is revised, and bridged representations can be double-counted by any aggregator.

stability.run_length.v1.title: Stable for N days (behaviour clock)
stability.run_length.v1.window: the agent's whole counted history, one value per complete UTC day
stability.run_length.v1.definition: For each agent at L7 or above, the number of complete UTC days since the last break in its own payment behaviour. A break is a day on which a two-sided CUSUM (reference 0.5, decision 4.74) on any of four daily features of its counted payments (payments, USD, distinct payees, share of payees never paid before; counts and USD on a log1p scale) crosses the decision threshold against the median and MAD of the agent's own previous days in the current regime (at most 60), with the MAD floored at 1.0 (0.25 for the share). A break restarts the baseline, so the new behaviour becomes the norm it is next judged against. The clock starts 14 days after the agent's first counted payment.
stability.run_length.v1.method: afg-stability, daily at 02:20 UTC, queries over money_events only. The decision threshold gives a one-sided average run length of about 730 days under Gaussian noise (Siegmund's approximation), about one false break per agent-year two-sided; payment counts are not Gaussian, so the measured break rate is published beside the designed one (false_alarm in /api/stability). A single large payment moves the statistic for one day and washes out: it is a point anomaly, not a regime.
excludes: Agents below L7, and agents with fewer than 15 complete days since their first counted payment (reported as too new).
Today's partial day.
does_not_assert: That a break is a harm: it is a change in the agent's own behaviour, which a new customer, a price change or a drain can all cause.
That the designed false-alarm rate holds: the measured rate is the honest one and is published.

survival.landmark.v1.title: Survival figures re-checked at a landmark (immortal-time bias)
survival.landmark.v1.window: 365 days from mint (first payment); days 60 to 90 from mint (early payers)
survival.landmark.v1.definition: Two checks of rank.survival.km.v1 against immortal-time bias (Cui 2022 §5.3). (1) The published figure groups identities by the total number of registrations their minter ever minted, which includes mints after the identity's own; the landmark figure groups by what was knowable at mint time: whether the minter had minted nothing before (first_of_minter) or at least 1,000 before (after_1000_of_minter). Both are Kaplan-Meier probabilities of a first counted payment within 365 days, and the two ratios are published side by side. (2) early_payers: at a landmark seven days after the mint, identities that had made a counted payment by then against those that had not, read on whether they made a counted payment in days 60-90; identities at least 90 days old only.
survival.landmark.v1.method: afg-ladderdyn, daily, queries only. When the two ratios differ by more than a quarter the landmark figure is the one to quote; the document says which case holds.
excludes: Identities younger than 90 days (early_payers).
Chains other than Base.
does_not_assert: That early payers are better agents: that they kept paying is what is measured.

treasury.share.cash.v1.title: Treasury share in stablecoins
treasury.share.cash.v1.definition: Stablecoins (USDC, USDT, EURC, DAI, USDbC) as a share of treasury.usd.total.v1.

sweep.watched.v1.title: Wallets swept every three hours
sweep.watched.v1.definition: Bound wallets whose outgoing USDC, USDT, EURC and DAI Transfer events are read every three hours.
sweep.watched.v1.method: eth_getLogs with the sender topic set to 2,000 wallets at a time, from the last swept block to the head. A wallet that moved money is queued for the per-wallet payment scan, which reads what it paid and checks the receipt.
excludes: Assets other than the four stablecoins.
does_not_assert: That a transfer is a payment. The sweep only decides who is read; the payment scan and the receipt check decide what counts.

treasury.share.defi.v1.title: Treasury share in DeFi positions
treasury.share.defi.v1.definition: Recognised DeFi receipts (lending supply tokens, vault shares), net of recognised debt tokens, as a share of treasury.usd.total.v1.
treasury.share.defi.v1.method: Recognised by token name and symbol against a short published list (Aave, Morpho, Moonwell, Compound, Euler, Fluid, Spark, Beefy, Yearn); anything else priced is a token.
excludes: Positions the list does not recognise, which fall into tokens.
does_not_assert: The yield earned.

sumlog.v1.title: Verifiable counted total (Merkle-sum log)
sumlog.v1.window: all counted payments at the time of the head
sumlog.v1.definition: Every counted payment (receipt read, after registration, not a routing hop: the set behind observed_pay_usd) is a leaf of a Merkle-sum tree in block order: leaf = SHA-256(0x00 || uint64be(amount_micro) || event_id|agent|to|amount_micro|block_epoch); node = SHA-256(0x01 || left || right || uint64be(left_sum) || uint64be(right_sum)), sum = left + right; RFC 6962 shape. The signed head carries the root, the total, and the root of a second tree whose leaves are each agent's own (root, sum, count), whose total must equal the first. A proof of one payment, or of one agent's record, recomputes the root and the total from the leaf up.
sumlog.v1.method: afg-sumlog, daily at 04:10 UTC; Ed25519 signature over afg-sum-log:v1:<leaves>:<root>:<sum_micro>:<agent_root>:<agents>:<timestamp_ms> with the published key. The counted set is not strictly append-only (a routing-hop re-check hours later, a late-found old payment), so every head states how many of the previous head's leaves are unchanged in order, changed, removed and added, and every agent record states the same for that agent. Proofs: /api/sum-log?event= and ?agent=; the hash levels are also served as 256-node tiles.
excludes: Payments whose receipt is not read yet, routing hops, and payments before registration (none of them is in the counted set).
does_not_assert: That the chain facts behind a leaf are right: the log proves what we published, and each leaf names the receipt to re-derive it from.
Append-only across heads: the numbers in the head say what changed.

treasury.share.eth.v1.title: Treasury share in ETH
treasury.share.eth.v1.definition: ETH, WETH and liquid-staking ETH tokens as a share of treasury.usd.total.v1.

treasury.usd.total.v1.title: What ranked agents hold
treasury.usd.total.v1.definition: The priced holdings of wallets bound to agents at L7 or above: stablecoins, ETH and ETH-like tokens, recognised DeFi positions net of recognised debt, and other tokens with a market price.
treasury.usd.total.v1.method: Balances from alchemy_getTokenBalances and eth_getBalance; prices from Alchemy's Prices API, refreshed daily. A wallet bound to several agents is counted once.
excludes: Tokens without a price (mostly airdropped spam): counted, never valued.
NFTs and positions held outside the wallet.
does_not_assert: That the tokens could be sold at that price.

treasury.share.tokens.v1.title: Treasury share in other tokens
treasury.share.tokens.v1.definition: Priced tokens that are not stablecoins, ETH or recognised DeFi positions, as a share of treasury.usd.total.v1.
excludes: Unpriced tokens.

tvl.total.v1.title: DeFi TVL, sum of chains
tvl.total.v1.definition: The sum of DefiLlama's per-chain TVL figures (its /v2/chains endpoint) at the time of reading. This is the 'TVL by chain' universe, which is smaller than the headline total on DefiLlama's home page: that headline adds categories the per-chain figures leave out (liquid staking, double-counted deposits, borrowed value) when its toggles are on. On 27 September 2026 the two read $96B and $126B for the same moment.
tvl.total.v1.method: Read from DefiLlama's chains endpoint every few minutes and summed. Not reproduced.
excludes: Liquid staking, double counting and borrowed value, which the per-chain figures exclude by DefiLlama's default.
Whatever else DefiLlama's methodology excludes; theirs is the definition here, not ours.
does_not_assert: Any connection to agents. Pure market context.

usdc.base.native.v1.title: Native USDC on Base
usdc.base.native.v1.definition: Supply of Circle-issued native USDC on Base.
excludes: Bridged USDC representations, which are a different asset with a different issuer risk.
does_not_assert: That this is agent money. It is the pool on the chain we measure agents on.

tvl.base.v1.title: DeFi TVL on Base
tvl.base.v1.definition: Total value locked on Base as reported by DefiLlama.
excludes: Other chains.
does_not_assert: Any connection to agents.

treasury.wallets.read.v1.title: Agent treasuries read
treasury.wallets.read.v1.definition: Wallets bound to agents at L7 or above whose full ERC-20 and ETH holdings were read.
treasury.wallets.read.v1.method: alchemy_getTokenBalances per wallet, ETH from a public node, prices from Alchemy's Prices API by token address.
does_not_assert: That the holdings belong to the agent rather than its operator.

usdc.share.v1.title: USDC share of stablecoin float
usdc.share.v1.definition: Circulating USDC divided by total stablecoin float.
usdc.share.v1.method: Arithmetic on the two DefiLlama figures above.
does_not_assert: That agent payments split the same way. They do not — agent payment volume we observe is overwhelmingly USDC, far above USDC's share of float, and conflating the two would misstate both.

usdc.circulating.v1.title: USDC in circulation
usdc.circulating.v1.definition: Circulating USDC supply across all chains, as reported by DefiLlama.
usdc.circulating.v1.method: Read from DefiLlama. Not reproduced by us.
excludes: Non-USDC stablecoins.
does_not_assert: That agents hold any particular share of it.

usdt.circulating.v1.title: USDT in circulation
usdt.circulating.v1.definition: Circulating USDT supply across all chains, as reported by DefiLlama.
usdt.circulating.v1.method: Read from DefiLlama. Not reproduced by us.
excludes: Non-USDT stablecoins.
does_not_assert: That USDT is used by agents. In our own payment observations it barely appears; it is published so the USDC share below has a denominator a reader can check.

wallet.7702.delegated.v1.title: Bound wallets delegated under EIP-7702
wallet.7702.delegated.v1.window: most recent code read per wallet
wallet.7702.delegated.v1.definition: Bound wallets whose on-chain code is exactly the EIP-7702 delegation designator 0xef0100 followed by a 20-byte implementation address.
wallet.7702.delegated.v1.method: eth_getCode per wallet. The designator is 23 bytes and nothing else in Ethereum produces that shape, so this is read, never inferred.
excludes: Wallets whose code we failed to read — they are not counted as undelegated, they are simply not counted.
does_not_assert: That the delegation is malicious, or that the implementation is a 'god key'. Unknown is not the same as unsafe; see the curated allowlist, which ships empty.

wallet.7702.impls.v1.title: Distinct EIP-7702 implementations in use
wallet.7702.impls.v1.definition: How many distinct implementation contracts the delegated wallets point at.
wallet.7702.impls.v1.method: Read the implementation address out of each delegation designator and count distinct values.
excludes: Wallets that have not delegated.
does_not_assert: That each implementation is a different codebase. Two addresses can hold identical bytecode.

vault.ixs.totalassets.v1.title: Agent-accessible vault cash
vault.ixs.totalassets.v1.definition: Total assets held by the tracked ERC-4626 agent vault, read from the contract.
vault.ixs.totalassets.v1.method: eth_call of totalAssets() against the vault. This one number is ours, read from the chain rather than taken from a dashboard.
excludes: Every other vault. This is one contract, not a category total.
does_not_assert: That the deposits belong to agents. A vault does not record whether its depositor is a person or a program, and we do not infer it.

wallet.7702.rate.v1.title: Share of examined wallets that have delegated
wallet.7702.rate.v1.definition: Wallets carrying an EIP-7702 delegation designator, divided by wallets whose code we read.
wallet.7702.rate.v1.method: A delegated account's code is exactly 23 bytes: the 0xef0100 prefix followed by the implementation address. Anything else is not a delegation.
excludes: Wallets whose code we failed to read.
does_not_assert: That delegation is dangerous. It is how a wallet gets batching, sponsorship and session keys.
That the wallet's owner understands what the implementation does. That is the actual risk, and it is not measurable from the designator.

wallet.7702.top4share.v1.title: Share of delegated wallets on the four busiest implementations
wallet.7702.top4share.v1.definition: Delegated wallets pointing at any of the four most-used implementations, divided by all delegated wallets.
wallet.7702.top4share.v1.method: As above, taking the top four.
excludes: Undelegated wallets.
does_not_assert: That these four are related, or audited, or unaudited. We publish the concentration, not a judgement of the code.

wallet.7702.topshare.v1.title: Share of delegated wallets on the single busiest implementation
wallet.7702.topshare.v1.definition: Delegated wallets pointing at the most-used implementation, divided by all delegated wallets.
wallet.7702.topshare.v1.method: Group delegated wallets by implementation address and take the largest.
excludes: Undelegated wallets.
does_not_assert: That the leading implementation is unsafe. It asserts concentration: a bug in one contract would reach this share of delegated agent wallets at once, which is a systemic fact worth knowing regardless of that contract's quality.

wallet.code.examined.v1.title: Wallets whose code we have read
wallet.code.examined.v1.definition: Bound wallets for which we have successfully read the account's code.
wallet.code.examined.v1.method: eth_getCode per wallet. A failed read is recorded as a failure and the wallet is excluded from both numerator and denominator of the delegation rate — never silently assumed undelegated.
excludes: Wallets whose code we could not read.
does_not_assert: That code is static. Delegation can be set and revoked, which is why delegated wallets are re-read daily and undelegated ones weekly.

x402.payers.24h.v1.title: Unique x402 payers in 24 hours
x402.payers.24h.v1.definition: Distinct paying addresses reported by x402scan for the last day.
does_not_assert: That a payer is an agent, or that one address is one party.

x402.observed.share.v1.title: Share of observed agent payments on the x402 rail
x402.observed.share.v1.definition: Of the payments we have observed leaving bound agent wallets, the share that landed on an address publicly indexed as an x402 payment recipient.

Until 2026-09-18 the harvest re-read only the first 2,000 of roughly 51,000 listings, so earlier values undercount more heavily and the step up on that date is coverage, not growth.
That a payment to an indexed recipient used the x402 protocol. The address is strong evidence of the rail, not proof of the handshake.

x402.settle.submitter.v1.title: Who submits x402 settlements
x402.settle.submitter.v1.unit: shares of settlements in the last 24 hours
x402.settle.submitter.v1.window: rolling 24 hours, up to 2,500 transactions read per run
x402.settle.submitter.v1.definition: Stablecoin transfers into the payTo addresses listed in the x402 Bazaar, each transaction read for its sender and function. An authorisation (transferWithAuthorization or receiveWithAuthorization, EIP-3009) submitted by the payer itself is self; by a sender that landed authorisations for at least 5 different sellers in the window is facilitator; by anyone else is third_party. A plain transfer by the payer is payer_transfer; a 4337 bundle or a smart-account execute is bundler_or_smart_account. receive_share is the share of authorisations in the closed form, which binds the submitter to the payee.
x402.settle.submitter.v1.method: afg-x402submit, daily at 04:40 UTC: eth_getLogs for the transfers, then each transaction from free public nodes. third_party is the replacement front-run surface Bartoletti & Zunino (2023) and Materwala et al. (2024) describe: an authorisation the payer signed, landed by a sender that is neither the payer nor a facilitator; it is also what a seller's own relayer looks like.
excludes: Sellers not listed in the Bazaar.
Transfers beyond the per-run cap (the document says how many were found and how many read).
does_not_assert: That a third-party submission was hostile: the list is transactions to read, not a verdict.

x402.settle.submitter.v2.title: Who submits x402 settlements
x402.settle.submitter.v2.unit: shares of settlements in the last 24 hours
x402.settle.submitter.v2.window: rolling 24 hours, up to 2,500 transactions read per run
x402.settle.submitter.v2.definition: Stablecoin transfers into the payTo addresses listed in the x402 Bazaar, each transaction read for its sender and function. An authorisation (transferWithAuthorization or receiveWithAuthorization, EIP-3009) counts whether it is called directly or inside a batch: when the outer call is not one of the known functions, the receipt is read, and an AuthorizationUsed on the token with the payer as authorizer makes it a batched authorisation. An authorisation submitted by the payer itself is self; by a sender that landed authorisations for at least 5 different sellers in the window is facilitator; by anyone else is third_party. A plain transfer by the payer is payer_transfer; a 4337 bundle or a smart-account execute is bundler_or_smart_account. receive_share is the share of authorisations in the closed form, which binds the submitter to the payee; batched authorisations are not counted in it because the receipt does not say which of the two functions was called.
x402.settle.submitter.v2.method: afg-x402submit, daily at 04:40 UTC: eth_getLogs for the transfers, then each transaction from free public nodes, and the receipt for a transaction whose outer function is not known. third_party is the replacement front-run surface Bartoletti & Zunino (2023) and Materwala et al. (2024) describe: an authorisation the payer signed, landed by a sender that is neither the payer nor a facilitator; it is also what a seller's own relayer, or a small facilitator below the 5-seller threshold, looks like.
excludes: Sellers not listed in the Bazaar.
Transfers beyond the per-run cap (the document says how many were found and how many read).
does_not_assert: That a third-party submission was hostile: the list is transactions to read, not a verdict.
That a sender below the 5-seller threshold is not a facilitator: the threshold is per window, and a facilitator serving few sellers that day is counted as third_party.

xchain.bnb.sample.paying.30d.v1.title: Share of sampled BNB registration owners that sent stablecoins, last 30 days
xchain.bnb.sample.paying.30d.v1.definition: Of a fixed random sample of 5,000 owner wallets, drawn once on 3 Oct 2026 as the owners of xchain.bnb.owner.wallets.v1 with the lowest sha256 of their lowercase address, and stored, the share that sent at least one transfer above zero of USDT, USDC, FDUSD and USD1 on BNB Smart Chain (18 decimals each, checked on chain on 3 Oct 2026), at one dollar to a different address in the last 30 days, counting only transfers after the owner's first registration on BNB. Published only once the sample's scan has reached the chain head.
xchain.bnb.sample.paying.30d.v1.method: Transfer logs of the four tokens with the sender topic set to the sampled owners, 1,000 per eth_getLogs, window by window from a cursor.
excludes: Owners outside the sample.
Transfers before the owner's first registration, to itself, or to burn addresses.
does_not_assert: That a transfer is a purchase or agent spending: no receipt check runs on BNB.
That an owner is an agent.

xchain.registrations.v1.title: ERC-8004 registrations on other chains
xchain.registrations.v1.definition: Registrations in the ERC-8004 Identity registry at the same address on Ethereum, Arbitrum One, OP Mainnet and Polygon PoS, with a current owner.
xchain.registrations.v1.method: Alchemy NFT API getOwnersForContract per chain, daily.
excludes: Base, which is counted separately and never added to this.
does_not_assert: That a registration is an operating agent.

xchain.owners.paying.30d.v1.title: Owners sending stablecoins on other chains, 30 days
xchain.owners.paying.30d.v1.definition: Owner wallets from xchain.owner.wallets.v1 that registered at least one agent themselves and sent USDC, bridged USDC or USDT to another address in the last 30 days, at or after the block of their own first registration on that chain.
xchain.owners.paying.30d.v1.method: eth_getLogs with the sender topic set to 1,000 owners at a time, per chain, from a cursor. An owner qualifies when it is the recipient of at least one of the registry's own mints (Transfer from the zero address).
excludes: Transfers before the owner's own first registration on that chain.
Self-transfers.

Wallets that only hold registrations someone else minted: an unsolicited transfer or airdrop of a registration does not make a wallet an agent owner (since 3 Oct 2026; on that day this removed 558 of 887 wallets on these four chains, most of them recipients of spam registrations on Ethereum).
does_not_assert: That a transfer is a purchase: these are not yet receipt-checked for routing hops the way Base payments are, so they are published as transfers, not as agent spending.
